śatrubhirjāyate yuddhaṃ divā naktaṃ dvijottamāḥ..9..
5.117.d:
तस्य वैरं समुत्पन्नं बहुभिः सह भूमिपैः ..
ततो निर्वास्यते देशो नीयते पशवो बलात् ..
शत्रुभिर्जायते युद्धं दिवा नक्तं द्विजोत्तमाः..9..
5.117.m: Enmity arose between him and many kings. / Then the land was ravaged, cattle were carried off by force, / and battle with enemies took place day and night, O best of brahmins.

5.117.s:
tataḥ katipayāhasya tasya bhāryā priyaṃvadā ..
ṛtusnātā dadhārātha garbhaṃ puṇyaṃ nijodare..6.118.10....
5.117.d:
ततः कतिपयाहस्य तस्य भार्या प्रियंवदा ..
ऋतुस्नाता दधाराथ गर्भं पुण्यं निजोदरे..6.118.10....
5.117.m: Then, after a few days, his wife Priyaṃvadā, / having bathed after her season, conceived a meritorious embryo in her womb.

5.117.s:
yataḥ prabhṛti tasyāḥ sa garbho'bhūdudarāśrayaḥ..
tataḥ prabhṛti rāṣṭrasya kṣemaṃ jātaṃ tathā pure......
eke saṃkhye jitā stena śatravo'pi sudurjayāḥ ..
nihatāśca tathaivānye mitrabhāvaṃ samāśritāḥ .. 12..
tato jajñe śubhā kanyā tasyāḥ padmāyatekṣaṇā..
aṃdhakāre'pi yadrātryāṃ dyotitaṃ sūtikāgṛham...3..
athā'sau pārthivaścakre sutavatsumahotsavam..
tasyāstoṣasamāyukto gītavādyādinisvanaiḥ ...4..
dine trayodaśe prāpte nāma tasyā yathocitam..
vihitaṃ bhūbhujā tena viprāṇāṃ purato dvijāḥ ...5..
yasmātkṣemaṃ samutpannaṃ garbhavāse'pi saṃsthayā ..
anayā kṣemaṃkarīnāma tasmādeṣābhave ddvijāḥ ...6..
evaṃ suvihitā khyātā vṛddhiṃ yāti dinedine ..
śuklapakṣe kalā cendoryathaiva gaganāṃgaṇe...7..
5.117.d:
यतः प्रभृति तस्याः स गर्भोऽभूदुदराश्रयः..
ततः प्रभृति राष्ट्रस्य क्षेमं जातं तथा पुरे......
एके संख्ये जिता स्तेन शत्रवोऽपि सुदुर्जयाः ..
निहताश्च तथैवान्ये मित्रभावं समाश्रिताः .. 12..
ततो जज्ञे शुभा कन्या तस्याः पद्मायतेक्षणा..
अंधकारेऽपि यद्रात्र्यां द्योतितं सूतिकागृहम्...3..
अथाऽसौ पार्थिवश्चक्रे सुतवत्सुमहोत्सवम्..
तस्यास्तोषसमायुक्तो गीतवाद्यादिनिस्वनैः ...4..
दिने त्रयोदशे प्राप्ते नाम तस्या यथोचितम्..
विहितं भूभुजा तेन विप्राणां पुरतो द्विजाः ...5..
यस्मात्क्षेमं समुत्पन्नं गर्भवासेऽपि संस्थया ..
अनया क्षेमंकरीनाम तस्मादेषाभवे द्द्विजाः ...6..
एवं सुविहिता ख्याता वृद्धिं याति दिनेदिने ..
शुक्लपक्षे कला चेन्दोर्यथैव गगनांगणे...7..
5.117.m:
From the time that embryo took abode in her womb, / from that time on welfare arose for the realm as well as in the city. / Some enemies, even though very hard to conquer, were defeated by him in battle; / others were slain, and still others sought friendship.
Then an auspicious daughter with eyes long like lotus petals was born to her, / who illuminated the lying-in chamber even in the darkness of night.
Then that king, filled with satisfaction, celebrated a great festival / for her, as if for a son, with the sounds of singing, instrumental music, and the like.
When the thirteenth day arrived, an appropriate name for her / was given by that monarch before the brahmins, O brahmins:
"Since welfare arose because of her staying even in the dwelling of the womb, / therefore, O brahmins, let her name be Kṣemaṃkarī."
Having thus been properly named and celebrated, she grew day by day, / just like a digit of the moon in the courtyard of the sky during the bright fortnight.

5.117.s:
tatastāṃ yauvanopetāṃ raivatāya mahīpatiḥ ..
dadau saurāṣṭranāthāya kāle vaivāhike śubhe .. 18 ..
atha tābhyāṃ sutā jātā revatīnāma viśrutā ..
bhaṭṭikāśāpadoṣeṇa śeṣapatnī yaśasvinī ...9..
5.117.d:
ततस्तां यौवनोपेतां रैवताय महीपतिः ..
ददौ सौराष्ट्रनाथाय काले वैवाहिके शुभे .. 18 ..
अथ ताभ्यां सुता जाता रेवतीनाम विश्रुता ..
भट्टिकाशापदोषेण शेषपत्नी यशस्विनी ...9..
5.117.m:
Then, when she attained youth, the king gave her / to Raivata, the lord of Saurāṣṭra, at an auspicious time for marriage.
Then from the two of them a daughter was born, known by the name Revatī, / the glorious wife of Śeṣa due to the fault of Bhaṭṭikā's curse,

5.117.s:
yā tūḍhā rāmarūpeṇa nāgarājena dhīmatā ..
putrapautravatī jātā saubhāgyamadagarvitā .. 6.118.20 ..
5.117.d:
या तूढा रामरूपेण नागराजेन धीमता ..
पुत्रपौत्रवती जाता सौभाग्यमदगर्विता .. 6.118.20 ..
5.117.m: who was married by the wise king of snakes in the form of Rāma; / she was blessed with sons and grandsons, proud with the joy of good fortune.

5.117.s:
na ca tābhyāṃ suto jātaḥ kathaṃcidapi vaṃśajaḥ ..
vayasoṃ'te'pi vipreṃdrāstato duḥkhaṃ vyajāyata .. 21 ..
5.117.d:
न च ताभ्यां सुतो जातः कथंचिदपि वंशजः ..
वयसोंऽतेऽपि विप्रेंद्रास्ततो दुःखं व्यजायत .. 21 ..
5.117.m: Yet no son was born from the two of them to continue the lineage, / even at the end of their age, O best of brahmins; from that arose sorrow.

5.117.s:
atha tau maṃtrivargasya rājyaṃ sarvamaśeṣataḥ ..
arpayitvā tu putrārthaṃ tapo'rthamiha cāgatau .. .. 22 ..
5.117.d:
अथ तौ मंत्रिवर्गस्य राज्यं सर्वमशेषतः ..
अर्पयित्वा तु पुत्रार्थं तपोऽर्थमिह चागतौ .. .. 22 ..
5.117.m: Then the two, having entrusted the entire kingdom / completely to the assembly of ministers, came here for the sake of a son and for austerity.

5.117.s:
tataḥ svamāśramaṃ gatvā sthitau tatra samāhitau ..
devīṃ kātyāyanīṃ sthāpya tadārādhanatatparau .. 23 ..
5.117.d:
ततः स्वमाश्रमं गत्वा स्थितौ तत्र समाहितौ ..
देवीं कात्यायनीं स्थाप्य तदाराधनतत्परौ .. 23 ..
5.117.m: Then, having gone to their own hermitage, they remained there composed, / having installed the goddess Kātyāyanī, intent upon worshipping her,

5.117.s:
yayā vinihato raudro mahiṣākhyo mahāsuraḥ ..
kaumāravratadhāriṇyā tasminvindhye mahācale .. 24 ..
5.117.d:
यया विनिहतो रौद्रो महिषाख्यो महासुरः ..
कौमारव्रतधारिण्या तस्मिन्विन्ध्ये महाचले .. 24 ..
5.117.m: by whom the terrible, great Asura named Mahiṣa had been slain / while she observed the vow of maidenhood on that great mountain Vindhya.

5.117.s:
tatastābhyāṃ dadau tuṣṭā sā putraṃ vaṃśavardhanam ..
nāmnā kṣemajitaṃ khyātaṃ parapakṣakṣayā vaham .. 25 ..
5.117.d:
ततस्ताभ्यां ददौ तुष्टा सा पुत्रं वंशवर्धनम् ..
नाम्ना क्षेमजितं ख्यातं परपक्षक्षया वहम् .. 25 ..
5.117.m: Then, pleased, she gave to the two a son who increased their lineage, / renowned by the name Kṣemajit, who brought about the destruction of the enemy faction.

5.117.s:
tataḥ svaṃ rājyamāsādya bhūyo'pi sa mahīpatiḥ ...
svaputraṃ vardhayāmāsa harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ .. 26 ..
5.117.d:
ततः स्वं राज्यमासाद्य भूयोऽपि स महीपतिः ...
स्वपुत्रं वर्धयामास हर्षेण महतान्वितः .. 26 ..
5.117.m: Then, having returned to his own kingdom, that king once again / raised his own son, filled with great joy.

5.117.s:
yadā sa yauvanopetaḥ sañjātaḥ kṣemajitsutaḥ ..
taṃ ca rājye niyojyā'tha svasthānaṃ sa punaryayau .. 27 ..
5.117.d:
यदा स यौवनोपेतः सञ्जातः क्षेमजित्सुतः ..
तं च राज्ये नियोज्याऽथ स्वस्थानं स पुनर्ययौ .. 27 ..
5.117.m: When that son, Kṣemajit, had attained youth, / he appointed him to the kingdom and then went once again to his own place,

5.117.s:
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ tadetaddvijasattamāḥ ..
bhāryayā sahitastyaktvā śeṣamanyaṃ paricchadam .. 28 ..
5.117.d:
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं तदेतद्द्विजसत्तमाः ..
भार्यया सहितस्त्यक्त्वा शेषमन्यं परिच्छदम् .. 28 ..
5.117.m: the sacred field arisen from Hāṭakeśvara, O best of brahmins, / together with his wife, having abandoned all other belongings.

5.117.s:
tatra saṃsthāpayāmāsa liṃgaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ ..
prāsādaṃ ca manohāri tataścakre samāhitaḥ.. 29
5.117.d:
तत्र संस्थापयामास लिंगं देवस्य शूलिनः ..
प्रासादं च मनोहारि ततश्चक्रे समाहितः.. 29
5.117.m: There he established a liṅga of the trident-bearing god, / and then, concentrated in mind, built a delightful temple,

5.117.s:
raivateśvaramityuktaṃ sarvapātaka nāśanam ..
darśanādeva sarveṣāṃ dehināṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 6.118.30 ..
5.117.d:
रैवतेश्वरमित्युक्तं सर्वपातक नाशनम् ..
दर्शनादेव सर्वेषां देहिनां द्विजसत्तमाः .. 6.118.30 ..
5.117.m: called Raivateśvara, which destroys all sins / merely by being seen by any embodied beings, O best of brahmins.

5.117.s:
yā pūrvaṃ sthāpitā durgā tasminkṣetre mahībhujā ..
tasyāḥ kṣemaṃkarī cakre prāsādaṃ śraddha yānvitā .. 31 ..
5.117.d:
या पूर्वं स्थापिता दुर्गा तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे महीभुजा ..
तस्याः क्षेमंकरी चक्रे प्रासादं श्रद्ध यान्विता .. 31 ..
5.117.m: To the Durgā who had previously been established in that sacred field by the king, / Kṣemaṃkarī built a temple, endowed with faith.

5.117.s:
sāpi kṣemaṃkarīnāma tataḥ prabhṛti kīrtyate ..
kātyāyanyapi yā proktā mahiṣāsuramardinī .. 32 ..
5.117.d:
सापि क्षेमंकरीनाम ततः प्रभृति कीर्त्यते ..
कात्यायन्यपि या प्रोक्ता महिषासुरमर्दिनी .. 32 ..
5.117.m: From that time forward she also is celebrated by the name Kṣemaṃkarī, / who is also declared to be Kātyāyanī, the slayer of Mahiṣāsura.

5.117.s:
yastāṃ caitrasite pakṣe saṃpa śyedaṣṭamīdine ..
tasyābhīṣṭā bhavetsiddhiḥ sarvadaiva dvijottamāḥ .. 33 ..
5.117.d:
यस्तां चैत्रसिते पक्षे संप श्येदष्टमीदिने ..
तस्याभीष्टा भवेत्सिद्धिः सर्वदैव द्विजोत्तमाः .. 33 ..
5.117.m: Whoever sees her on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, / their desired perfection shall always come to pass, O best of brahmins.

5.117.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ raivateśvaravarṇanam ..
kṣemaṃkaryāḥ prabhāvaṃ ca sarvapātakanāśanam .. 34 ..
5.117.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं रैवतेश्वरवर्णनम् ..
क्षेमंकर्याः प्रभावं च सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 34 ..
5.117.m: This has all been related to you: the description of Raivateśvara, / and the power of Kṣemaṃkarī, which destroys all sins.

5.117.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyā ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye kṣemaṃkarīraivateśvarotpattitīrtha māhātmyavarṇananāmāṣṭādaśottaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 118 .. ..
5.117.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहिताया षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये क्षेमंकरीरैवतेश्वरोत्पत्तितीर्थ माहात्म्यवर्णननामाष्टादशोत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 118 .. ..
5.117.m: Thus ends the one hundred and eighteenth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Māhātmya of the Sacred Ford of the Origin of Kṣemaṃkarī and Raivateśvara,' in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth section in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.118.s:
.. ..ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yatvayā sūtaja proktaṃ devī kātyāyanī ca sā ..
mahiṣāṃtakarī jātā kathaṃ sā me prakīrtaya.....
kīdṛgdānavavaryaḥ sa māhiṣaṃ rūpamāśritaḥ ..
kasmātsa sūdito devyā tanme vistarato vada ..2..
5.118.d:
.. ..ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यत्वया सूतज प्रोक्तं देवी कात्यायनी च सा ..
महिषांतकरी जाता कथं सा मे प्रकीर्तय.....
कीदृग्दानववर्यः स माहिषं रूपमाश्रितः ..
कस्मात्स सूदितो देव्या तन्मे विस्तरतो वद ..2..
5.118.m: The seers said: / That which was told by you, O son of Sūta, that the goddess Kātyāyanī / became the slayer of Mahiṣa—proclaim to me how that was. / What kind of foremost Dānava was he who assumed the form of a buffalo? / Why was he slain by the goddess? Tell me that in detail.

5.118.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi devyā māhātmyamuttamam ..
śrutamātre'pi martyānāṃ yena śatrukṣayo bhavet .. 3 ..
5.118.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अत्र वः कीर्तयिष्यामि देव्या माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ..
श्रुतमात्रेऽपि मर्त्यानां येन शत्रुक्षयो भवेत् .. 3 ..
5.118.m: Sūta said: / In this regard I shall proclaim to you the supreme māhātmya of the goddess, / merely by the hearing of which the destruction of enemies occurs for mortals.

5.118.s:
hiraṇyākṣasutaḥ pūrvaṃ mahiṣonāma dānavaḥ ..
āsīnmahiṣarūpeṇa yena bhuktaṃ jagattrayam..4..
5.118.d:
हिरण्याक्षसुतः पूर्वं महिषोनाम दानवः ..
आसीन्महिषरूपेण येन भुक्तं जगत्त्रयम्..4..
5.118.m: Formerly, the son of Hiraṇyākṣa was a Dānava named Mahiṣa; / he was in the form of a buffalo, by whom the three worlds were enjoyed.

5.118.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
māhiṣeṇa svarūpeṇa kiṃjātaḥ sūtanaṃdana ..
athavā śāpadoṣeṇa sañjātaḥ kenacidvada ..5..
5.118.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
माहिषेण स्वरूपेण किंजातः सूतनंदन ..
अथवा शापदोषेण सञ्जातः केनचिद्वद ..5..
5.118.m: The seers said: / Was he born with the natural form of a buffalo, O delight of Sūta, / or was he born [such] through the fault of someone's curse? Tell us.

5.118.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
saṃjāto hi surūpāḍhyaḥ śatapatranibhānanaḥ ..
dīrghabāhuḥ pṛthugrīvaḥ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ ..
nāmnā citrasamaḥ proktastejovīryasamanvitaḥ . 6 ..
5.118.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
संजातो हि सुरूपाढ्यः शतपत्रनिभाननः ..
दीर्घबाहुः पृथुग्रीवः सर्वलक्षणलक्षितः ..
नाम्ना चित्रसमः प्रोक्तस्तेजोवीर्यसमन्वितः . 6 ..
5.118.m: Sūta said: / He was indeed born endowed with handsome form, with a face like a lotus, / long-armed, broad-necked, marked with all auspicious marks, / declared to be Citrasama by name, endowed with fiery splendor and vigor.

5.118.s:
sabālyātprabhṛti prāyo mahiṣāṇāṃ prabodhanam ..
karoti saṃparityajya sarvamaśvādivāhanam.. 7 ..
5.118.d:
सबाल्यात्प्रभृति प्रायो महिषाणां प्रबोधनम् ..
करोति संपरित्यज्य सर्वमश्वादिवाहनम्.. 7 ..
5.118.m: From childhood onwards, he mostly trained buffaloes, / abandoning all other mounts such as horses.

5.118.s:
kadācinmahiṣārūḍhaḥ sa pratasthe danoḥ sutaḥ ..
jāhnavītīramāsādya vinighnañjalapakṣiṇaḥ .. 9 ..
athāsītsusamādhistho durvāsā munisattamaḥ ..
gaṃgātīre vidhāyoccaiḥ padmā sanamanuttamam .. 9 ..
5.118.d:
कदाचिन्महिषारूढः स प्रतस्थे दनोः सुतः ..
जाह्नवीतीरमासाद्य विनिघ्नञ्जलपक्षिणः .. 9 ..
अथासीत्सुसमाधिस्थो दुर्वासा मुनिसत्तमः ..
गंगातीरे विधायोच्चैः पद्मा सनमनुत्तमम् .. 9 ..
5.118.m:
Once, mounted on a buffalo, that son of Danu set forth; / having reached the bank of the Jāhnavī, he was striking water birds.
Now Durvāsas, the best of sages, was situated in deep meditation, / having assumed a supreme lotus posture high upon the bank of the Gaṅgā.

5.118.s:
vihaṃgāsaktacittena śūnyena sa munīśvaraḥ ..
dṛṣṭo na mahiṣakṣuṇṇaḥ khurairvegavaśāddvijaḥ .. 6.119.10 ..
5.118.d:
विहंगासक्तचित्तेन शून्येन स मुनीश्वरः ..
दृष्टो न महिषक्षुण्णः खुरैर्वेगवशाद्द्विजः .. 6.119.10 ..
5.118.m: With his mind intent on the birds and distracted, that lord of sages / was not seen [by him]; the brahmin was trampled by the buffalo with its hooves due to its speed.

5.118.s:
tataḥ kṣatajadigdhāṃgaḥ sa dṛṣṭvā dānavaṃ puraḥ ..
atha dṛṣṭvā praṇāmena rahitaṃ kopamāviśat......
tataḥ provāca taṃ kruddhastoyamādāya pāṇinā ..
yasmātpāpa mama kṣuṇṇaṃ gātraṃ mahiṣajaiḥ khuraiḥ .. 12 ..
5.118.d:
ततः क्षतजदिग्धांगः स दृष्ट्वा दानवं पुरः ..
अथ दृष्ट्वा प्रणामेन रहितं कोपमाविशत्......
ततः प्रोवाच तं क्रुद्धस्तोयमादाय पाणिना ..
यस्मात्पाप मम क्षुण्णं गात्रं महिषजैः खुरैः .. 12 ..
5.118.m: Then, his limbs smeared with blood, seeing the Dānava before him, / and seeing that he was devoid of obeisance, he was overcome with anger. / Then, enraged, taking water in his hand, he said to him: / 'Since, O sinful one, my body was trampled by the hooves of a buffalo,

5.118.s:
samādheśca kṛto bhaṃgastasmāttvaṃ mahiṣo bhava ..
yāvajjīvasi durbuddhe samyagjñānasamanvitaḥ .. 13 ..
5.118.d:
समाधेश्च कृतो भंगस्तस्मात्त्वं महिषो भव ..
यावज्जीवसि दुर्बुद्धे सम्यग्ज्ञानसमन्वितः .. 13 ..
5.118.m: and the breaking of my meditation was caused, therefore become a buffalo / as long as you live, O evil-minded one, endowed with full consciousness!'

5.118.s:
athā'sau mahiṣo jātaḥ kṛṣṇagātradharo mahān ..
atidīrghaviṣāṇaśca aṃjanādririvāparaḥ .. 14 ..
5.118.d:
अथाऽसौ महिषो जातः कृष्णगात्रधरो महान् ..
अतिदीर्घविषाणश्च अंजनाद्रिरिवापरः .. 14 ..
5.118.m: Then he became a great buffalo, bearing a black body / and exceedingly long horns, like a second mountain of collyrium.

5.118.s:
tataḥ prasādayāmāsa taṃ muniṃ vinayānvitaḥ ..
śāpātaṃ kuru me vipra bālyabhāvādajānataḥ .. 15 ..
5.118.d:
ततः प्रसादयामास तं मुनिं विनयान्वितः ..
शापातं कुरु मे विप्र बाल्यभावादजानतः .. 15 ..
5.118.m: Then, endowed with humility, he propitiated that sage: / 'Bring an end to my curse, O brahmin; I did not know because of my childish state.'

5.118.s:
atha taṃ sa muniḥ prāha na me syādvacanaṃ vṛthā ..
tasmādyāvatsthitāḥ prāṇāstāvaditthaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 16 ..
5.118.d:
अथ तं स मुनिः प्राह न मे स्याद्वचनं वृथा ..
तस्माद्यावत्स्थिताः प्राणास्तावदित्थं भविष्यति .. 16 ..
5.118.m: Then that sage said to him: 'My word cannot be in vain; / therefore, as long as your life-breaths remain, it shall be so,

5.118.s:
mahiṣasya svarūpeṇa ninditasya sudurmate ..
evaṃ sa taṃ parityajya gaṃgātīraṃ munīśvaraḥ ..
jagāmā'nyatra so'pyāśu gatvā śukramuvāca ha .. 17 ..
5.118.d:
महिषस्य स्वरूपेण निन्दितस्य सुदुर्मते ..
एवं स तं परित्यज्य गंगातीरं मुनीश्वरः ..
जगामाऽन्यत्र सोऽप्याशु गत्वा शुक्रमुवाच ह .. 17 ..
5.118.m: in the form of a contemptible buffalo, O exceedingly evil-minded one!' / Having thus abandoned him on the bank of the Gaṅgā, the lord of sages / went elsewhere. He also, having gone quickly, spoke to Śukra:

5.118.s:
ahaṃ durvāsasā śaptaḥ kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare ..
mahiṣatvaṃ samānītastasmāttvaṃ me gatirbhava .. 18 ..
5.118.d:
अहं दुर्वाससा शप्तः कस्मिंश्चित्कारणांतरे ..
महिषत्वं समानीतस्तस्मात्त्वं मे गतिर्भव .. 18 ..
5.118.m: 'I was cursed by Durvāsas for a certain reason, / and brought to the state of a buffalo; therefore become my refuge.

5.118.s:
yathā syātpūrvajaṃ dehaṃ tiryaktvaṃ naśyate yathā ..
prasādāttava vipreṃdra tathā nītirvidhīyatām .. 19 ..
5.118.d:
यथा स्यात्पूर्वजं देहं तिर्यक्त्वं नश्यते यथा ..
प्रसादात्तव विप्रेंद्र तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् .. 19 ..
5.118.m: So that my previous body may return and my animal state may be destroyed / by your favor, O chief of brahmins, let an expedient be prescribed.'

5.118.s:
.. śukra uvāca .. ..
tasya śāpo'nyathā kartuṃ naiva śakyaḥ kathaṃcana ..
kenāpi saṃparityajya devamekaṃ maheśvaram .. 6.119.20 ..
5.118.d:
.. शुक्र उवाच .. ..
तस्य शापोऽन्यथा कर्तुं नैव शक्यः कथंचन ..
केनापि संपरित्यज्य देवमेकं महेश्वरम् .. 6.119.20 ..
5.118.m: Śukra said: / 'It is not possible in any way to alter his curse / by anyone, with the exception of the one god, Maheśvara.

5.118.s:
tasmādārādhayā''śu tvaṃ gatvā liṃgamanuttamam ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sarvasiddhipradāyake .. 21 ..
5.118.d:
तस्मादाराधया'ऽशु त्वं गत्वा लिंगमनुत्तमम् ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायके .. 21 ..
5.118.m: Therefore, having gone quickly, worship the unsurpassed liṅga / in the sacred field arisen from Hāṭakeśvara, which grants all perfections.

5.118.s:
tatra sañjāyate siddhiḥ śīghraṃ dānavasattama ..
api pāpayuge prāpte kiṃ punaḥ prathame yuge. 22 ..
5.118.d:
तत्र सञ्जायते सिद्धिः शीघ्रं दानवसत्तम ..
अपि पापयुगे प्राप्ते किं पुनः प्रथमे युगे. 22 ..
5.118.m: Perfection arises there quickly, O best of Dānavas, / even when the sinful age has arrived, how much more so in the first age?'

5.118.s:
evamuktaḥ sa śukreṇa dānavaḥ satvaraṃ yayau ..
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ tapastepe tataḥ param .. 23 ..
5.118.d:
एवमुक्तः स शुक्रेण दानवः सत्वरं ययौ ..
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं तपस्तेपे ततः परम् .. 23 ..
5.118.m: Thus addressed by Śukra, the Dānava swiftly went / to the sacred field arisen from Hāṭakeśvara; thereafter he performed austerity.

5.118.s:
sthāpayitvā mahalligaṃ bhaktyā devasya śūlinaḥ ..
prāsādaṃ ca tataścakre kailāsaśikharopamam .. 094 ..
tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya tapaḥsthasya mahātmanaḥ ..
jagāma sumahānkālaḥ kṛcchre tapasi vartataḥ .. 25 ..
tatastuṣṭo mahādevo gatvā taddṛṣṭigocaram ..
provāca parituṣṭo'smi varaṃ varaya dānava .. 26 ..
.. mahiṣa uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ durvāsasā śapto mahiṣatve niyojitaḥ ..
tiryaktvaṃ nāśamāyātu tasmānme tvatprasādataḥ .. 27 ..
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
nānyathā śakyate kartuṃ tasya vākyaṃ kathaṃcana ..

5.118.m:
Having installed a great liṅga of the trident-bearing god with devotion, / he then built a temple resembling a peak of Kailāsa.
As that great-souled one remained engaged in austerity in this manner, / a very long time passed while he persisted in severe austerity.
Then Mahādeva, pleased, came into the range of his vision / and said: “I am well pleased; choose a boon, O Dānava.”
Mahiṣa said: / “I was cursed by Durvāsas and forced into the state of a buffalo; / therefore, by your grace, let my animal nature come to an end.”
The Blessed Lord said: / “His word cannot be undone in any way; / therefore, I shall create a means of happiness for you. Hear it:
Whatever human pleasures there are, as well as divine and demonic ones, / all of them will find a dwelling here in your body.
Since a mortal body is desired by gods and demons for the sake of enjoyment, / you will attain them all; therefore, your body [will be endowed with all pleasures].”

5.118.m:
Mahiṣa said: / “If indeed, O Lord of the gods of gods, I am to attain enjoyments, / then let this body of mine be completely invulnerable to death, O Lord,
from the ten classes of divine beings, and especially from humans, / animals, snakes, and birds, O best of gods!”
The Blessed Lord said: / “No embodied being on the surface of the earth is entirely invulnerable to death, O Dānava. / Therefore, leave out one and ask regarding the rest, O lord of Daityas.”
Then, having reflected for a long time, he said to the one whose emblem is a bull: / “Except for a single woman, let there be no death for me from any others.
Likewise, whatever person, undisturbed, takes a bath with faith / here in my sacred ford and then looks upon you,
let there be for him, by your grace, the fulfillment of all desires, / the destruction of all afflictions, and an increase of fiery energy, O Śaṃkara.”
The Blessed Lord said: / “Whoever bathes here in your sacred ford on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa / and then gazes with love upon my liṅga,

Having spoken thus, the Lord of gods then vanished from sight. / Mahiṣa too then went to his own abode.
Having gone there and summoned all the Dānavas, / he, filled with rage, said in the midst of the assembly:
“My father, my uncle, and whatever other ancestors of mine [there were]— / those Dānavas were slain by the gods headed by Vāsudeva.
Therefore, I shall destroy those gods too in a great battle; / and after that I will seize the sovereignty over the three worlds.”
Then those Dānavas said: “This is fitting and most excellent; / this kingdom that Śakra exercises in heaven belongs to us.
Therefore, having gone swiftly this very day and slain Indra at the forefront of the battle, / we will dwell happily in heaven, enjoying celestial pleasures.”

5.118.m:
Thus, all those Dānavas, having made their counsel and decision, / went then to the peak of Meru, accompanied by servants, troops, and mounts.
Then Śakra and the other gods, seeing that army arising from the Dānavas / which had arrived all of a sudden, equipped with weapons and missiles, / went out immediately thereafter to the gate of their own city to fight:
the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Nāsatyas—the best of physicians— / the Viśvedevas, and likewise the Sādhyas, the Siddhas, and whatever Vidyādharas [there were].
Then a battle took place between the gods and the Dānavas, / who threatened each other and made death their only retreat.
Thus the battle went on in heaven for as long as three years; / very vast rivers of blood flowed exceedingly there.
On another day, seeing Śakra mounted upon Airāvaṇa, / with a white umbrella being held over his head, / and surrounded by gods with divine weapons in their hands,
Mahiṣa, the ruler of the Dānavas, his mind overcome with anger, / gathered great speed and charged directly facing him.

5.118.m:
And with his two very sharp horns he then pierced the elephant Airāvaṇa / in the chest; and the elephant let out a dreadful cry.
Then, turning away and intent on flight, / he ran swiftly toward where the city of Amarāvatī lay.
And though his frontal globes were wounded repeatedly by blows from the elephant-goad, / and though held back by the mahout, he would not stop in any way.
Then the thousand-eyed [Indra], seeing Mahiṣa proud / and the Daityas roaring with war-cries, clappings of arms, and the like, said:
“Do not think, O Daitya, that the lord of the thirty [gods] has fled; / this elephant, beyond my control, leaves the battle and goes away by force.
Therefore, wait a moment while, having mounted a fine chariot, / I destroy your pride by slaying [you] with sharp arrows.”
In the meantime, Mātali, Śakra’s charioteer, arrived / with a [chariot] yoked to ten thousand horses swift as the wind.
Those horses, struck by Mātali with the whip, / ran swiftly as if flying up into the sky.

ततस्तु दानवाः सर्वे भग्नान्दृष्ट्वा रणे सुरान्.
शस्त्रवृष्टिं प्रमुंचंतो गर्जमाना यथा घनाः..65..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्ता रजनी तमसावृता.
न किंचित्तत्र संयाति कस्यचिद्दृष्टिगोचरे..66..
ततस्तु दानवाः सर्वे युद्धान्निर्वृत्य सर्वतः.
मेरुशृंगं समाश्रित्य रम्यं वासं प्रचक्रमुः..67..
5.118.m:
Then Pākaśāsana, quickly stringing his bow, / covered the Dānava with arrows resembling venomous serpents.
Then he, gathering speed and once again fainting with rage, / rushed with velocity to where the lord of the thirty [gods] was.
Then, having gathered speed, enraged, whirling repeatedly, / he tore his fine horses with his two horns.
Then those frightened horses, their chests wounded / and their whole bodies bathed in blood, took the path of Airāvaṇa.
Then the best of gods, seeing Śakra’s chariot turned away, / all fled in terror, following his path.
Then all the Dānavas, seeing the gods broken in battle, / rained down a shower of weapons, roaring like clouds.
In the meantime, night shrouded in darkness arrived; / nothing there came into the range of anyone’s sight.
Then all the Dānavas, completely ceasing from the battle, / took shelter on the peak of Meru and made a delightful encampment.

5.118.s:
vijayena samāyuktāstuṣṭiṃ ca paramāṃ gatāḥ.
kathāścakruśca yuddhotthā yuddhaṃ tasya yathā bhavat..68..
devāścāpi hatotsāhāḥ prahāraiḥ kṣatavikṣatāḥ.
maṃtraṃ cakrurmitho bhūtvā bṛhaspatipuraḥsarāḥ..69..
sāṃprataṃ dānavaiḥ sainyamasmākaṃ vimukhaṃ kṛtam ..
vidhvastaṃ sunirutsāhamakṣamaṃ yuddhakarmaṇi .. 6.119.70 ..
tasmāttyaktvā pravekṣyāmaḥ purīṃ caivāmarāvatīm ..
brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ yatra na syāddānavajaṃ bhayam..7...
evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā brahmalokaṃ tato gatāḥ ..
śūnyāṃ śakrapurīṃ kṛtvā sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ..72..
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya dānavāste praharṣitāḥ ..
śūnyāṃ śakrapurīṃ dṛṣṭvā viviśustadanaṃtaram .. 73 ..
atha śākre pade daityaṃ mahiṣaṃ saṃnidhāya ca ..
praṇemustuṣṭisaṃyuktāścakruścaiva mahotsavam .. 74 ..
5.118.d:
विजयेन समायुक्तास्तुष्टिं च परमां गताः.
कथाश्चक्रुश्च युद्धोत्था युद्धं तस्य यथा भवत्..68..
देवाश्चापि हतोत्साहाः प्रहारैः क्षतविक्षताः.
मंत्रं चक्रुर्मिथो भूत्वा बृहस्पतिपुरःसराः..69..
सांप्रतं दानवैः सैन्यमस्माकं विमुखं कृतम् ..
विध्वस्तं सुनिरुत्साहमक्षमं युद्धकर्मणि .. 6.119.70 ..
तस्मात्त्यक्त्वा प्रवेक्ष्यामः पुरीं चैवामरावतीम् ..
ब्रह्मणः सदनं यत्र न स्याद्दानवजं भयम्..7...
एवं ते निश्चयं कृत्वा ब्रह्मलोकं ततो गताः ..
शून्यां शक्रपुरीं कृत्वा सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः..72..
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय दानवास्ते प्रहर्षिताः ..
शून्यां शक्रपुरीं दृष्ट्वा विविशुस्तदनंतरम् .. 73 ..
अथ शाक्रे पदे दैत्यं महिषं संनिधाय च ..
प्रणेमुस्तुष्टिसंयुक्ताश्चक्रुश्चैव महोत्सवम् .. 74 ..
5.118.m:
Endowed with victory and attaining the highest satisfaction, / they talked of the battle, of how his battle had unfolded.
And the gods too, their spirit broken, wounded and bruised by blows, / assembled together and deliberated, led by Bṛhaspati:
"Now our army has been turned back by the Dānavas, / shattered, utterly dispirited, and unable to fight.
Therefore, abandoning even the city of Amarāvatī, we will enter / the abode of Brahmā, where there will be no fear born of the Dānavas."
Having thus resolved, all the gods along with Indra / left the city of Śakra empty and then went to the world of Brahmā.
Then, rising at dawn, those Dānavas were exceedingly rejoiced; / seeing the city of Śakra empty, they entered it immediately thereafter.
Then, having established the Daitya Mahiṣa upon the seat of Indra, / they bowed down filled with satisfaction and celebrated a great festival.

5.118.s:
jagṛhuryajñabhāgāṃśca sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām ..
devasthāneṣu sarveṣu devatā'bhimatāśca ye .. 76 ..
5.118.d:
जगृहुर्यज्ञभागांश्च सर्वेषां त्रिदिवौकसाम् ..
देवस्थानेषु सर्वेषु देवताऽभिमताश्च ये .. 76 ..
5.118.m: And they seized the sacrificial shares of all the dwellers in heaven, / and whatever deities were revered in all the divine abodes.

5.118.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye devasenāparājayavarṇanaṃnāmaikonaviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 119 .. .. cha ..
5.118.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये देवसेनापराजयवर्णनंनामैकोनविंशत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 119 .. .. छ ..
5.118.m: Thus ends the one hundred and nineteenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Defeat of the Divine Army,' in the glorification of the sacred field of Śrī Hāṭakeśvara in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

5.119.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ śakrādayo devā jitāste tu raṇājire ..
mahiṣeṇa tato rājyaṃ trailokye'pi cakāra saḥ .. 1 ..
5.119.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं शक्रादयो देवा जितास्ते तु रणाजिरे ..
महिषेण ततो राज्यं त्रैलोक्येऽपि चकार सः .. 1 ..
5.119.m: Sūta said: / When the gods, Indra and the others, were thus conquered on the battlefield, / Mahiṣa then ruled even over the three worlds.

5.119.s:
yatkiñcittriṣu lokeṣu sārabhūtaṃ prapaśyati ..
gajavājirathāśvādi sarvaṃ gṛhṇāti so'suraḥ .. 2 ..
5.119.d:
यत्किञ्चित्त्रिषु लोकेषु सारभूतं प्रपश्यति ..
गजवाजिरथाश्वादि सर्वं गृह्णाति सोऽसुरः .. 2 ..
5.119.m: Whatever of supreme value he saw in the three worlds— / elephants, steeds, chariots, horses, and the like—that Asura seized it all.

5.119.s:
evaṃ pravartamānasya tasya devāḥ savāsavāḥ ..
vadhārthaṃ militāścakruḥ kathā duḥkhasama nvitāḥ .. 3 ..
5.119.d:
एवं प्रवर्तमानस्य तस्य देवाः सवासवाः ..
वधार्थं मिलिताश्चक्रुः कथा दुःखसम न्विताः .. 3 ..
5.119.m: While he was behaving thus, the gods along with Indra / gathered for the sake of his destruction and spoke words filled with sorrow.

5.119.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāpto nārado munisattamaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā taṃ māhiṣaṃ sarvaṃ vyavahāraṃ mahotkaṭam .. 4 ..
5.119.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तो नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ..
दृष्ट्वा तं माहिषं सर्वं व्यवहारं महोत्कटम् .. 4 ..
5.119.m: Meanwhile, the best of sages, Nārada, arrived there, / having seen all that excessive conduct of Mahiṣa.

5.119.s:
tataśca kathayāmāsa sarvaṃ teṣāṃ savista ram ..
tasya saṃceṣṭitaṃ bhūri lokatrayaprapīḍanam .. 5 ..
5.119.d:
ततश्च कथयामास सर्वं तेषां सविस्त रम् ..
तस्य संचेष्टितं भूरि लोकत्रयप्रपीडनम् .. 5 ..
5.119.m: And then he told them in full detail / of all his extensive deeds, which oppressed the three worlds.

5.119.s:
atha teṣāṃ mahākopo bhūya evābhyavardhata ..
nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā tādṛglokakathodbhavam .. .. 6 ..
5.119.d:
अथ तेषां महाकोपो भूय एवाभ्यवर्धत ..
नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा तादृग्लोककथोद्भवम् .. .. 6 ..
5.119.m: Then their great rage increased all the more, / having heard Nārada's words arising from such reports of the world.

5.119.s:
teṣāṃ kopodbhavo gharmo vaktradvāreṇa niryayau ..
yena diṅmaṃḍalaṃ sarvaṃ tatkṣaṇātkaluṣīkṛtam .. 7 ..
5.119.d:
तेषां कोपोद्भवो घर्मो वक्त्रद्वारेण निर्ययौ ..
येन दिङ्मंडलं सर्वं तत्क्षणात्कलुषीकृतम् .. 7 ..
5.119.m: From their mouths came forth heat born of their wrath, / by which the whole circle of the directions was instantly polluted.

5.119.s:
etasminnaṃtare tatra kārtikeyaḥ samabhyayāt ..
papraccha ca kimetaddhi devānāṃ kopakāraṇam ..
yena kāluṣyatāṃ prāptaṃ dikcakraṃ sakalaṃ mune .. ca ..
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
eteṣāṃ sāṃprataṃ skanda mayā vārtā niveditā ..
trailokyaṃ dānavaiḥ sarvairyathā nītaṃ madotkaṭaiḥ .. 9 ..
5.119.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र कार्तिकेयः समभ्ययात् ..
पप्रच्छ च किमेतद्धि देवानां कोपकारणम् ..
येन कालुष्यतां प्राप्तं दिक्चक्रं सकलं मुने .. च ..
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
एतेषां सांप्रतं स्कन्द मया वार्ता निवेदिता ..
त्रैलोक्यं दानवैः सर्वैर्यथा नीतं मदोत्कटैः .. 9 ..
5.119.m: At that moment Kārtikeya arrived there / and asked: "What is this cause of the anger of the gods, / by which, O sage, the entire circle of the directions has become clouded?" / Nārada said: / "O Skanda, news has now been reported by me to these [gods] / of how the three worlds have been seized by all the Dānavas, haughty with pride.

5.119.s:
strīratnamaśvaratnaṃ vā na kiṃcitkasyacidgṛhe ..
te dṛṣṭvā mokṣayaṃti sma durnivāryā madotkaṭāḥ .. 6.120.10 ..
5.119.d:
स्त्रीरत्नमश्वरत्नं वा न किंचित्कस्यचिद्गृहे ..
ते दृष्ट्वा मोक्षयंति स्म दुर्निवार्या मदोत्कटाः .. 6.120.10 ..
5.119.m: A jewel among women or a jewel among horses—there was nothing in anyone's house / that those insolent and uncontrollable ones did not plunder once they saw it."

5.119.s:
tacchrutvā kārtikeyasya viśeṣātsaṃprajāyata ..
vaktradvāreṇa devānāṃ yathā kopaḥ samāgataḥ .. 11 ..
5.119.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा कार्तिकेयस्य विशेषात्संप्रजायत ..
वक्त्रद्वारेण देवानां यथा कोपः समागतः .. 11 ..
5.119.m: Hearing that, [anger] arose especially in Kārtikeya, / just as the anger had come forth through the mouths of the gods.

5.119.s:
etasminnaṃtare jātā tatkopāṃte kumārikā ..
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannā divyatejo'nvitā śubhā .. 12 ..
5.119.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे जाता तत्कोपांते कुमारिका ..
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्ना दिव्यतेजोऽन्विता शुभा .. 12 ..
5.119.m: In that interval, at the end of that anger, a young maiden was born, / endowed with all auspicious marks, possessed of divine radiance, and auspicious.

5.119.s:
kārtikeyasya kopena kope miśre divaukasām ..
yasmājjātātra sā kanyā tasmātkātyāyanī smṛtā .. 13 ..
5.119.d:
कार्तिकेयस्य कोपेन कोपे मिश्रे दिवौकसाम् ..
यस्माज्जातात्र सा कन्या तस्मात्कात्यायनी स्मृता .. 13 ..
5.119.m: Because that maiden was born here from the anger of Kārtikeya / blended with the anger of the celestials, she is therefore called Kātyāyanī.

5.119.s:
tatastasyā dadau vajramāyudhaṃ tridaśādhipaḥ ..
śaktiṃ skandaḥ sutīkṣṇāgrāṃ cāpaṃ devo janārdanaḥ .. 14 ..
5.119.d:
ततस्तस्या ददौ वज्रमायुधं त्रिदशाधिपः ..
शक्तिं स्कन्दः सुतीक्ष्णाग्रां चापं देवो जनार्दनः .. 14 ..
5.119.m: Then the lord of the gods gave her his thunderbolt weapon; / Skanda [gave] a very sharp-pointed spear; the god Janārdana [gave] a bow;

5.119.s:
triśūlaṃ ca mahādevaḥ pāśaṃ ca varuṇaḥ svayam ..
ādityaśca sitānbāṇāṃścaṃdramāścarma cottamam .. 15 ..
5.119.d:
त्रिशूलं च महादेवः पाशं च वरुणः स्वयम् ..
आदित्यश्च सितान्बाणांश्चंद्रमाश्चर्म चोत्तमम् .. 15 ..
5.119.m: Mahādeva [gave] a trident, and Varuṇa himself a noose; / the Sun [gave] white arrows, and the Moon an excellent shield;

5.119.s:
nistriṃśaṃ nirṛtistuṣṭa ulmukaṃ ca hutāśanaḥ ..
vāyuśca cchurikāṃ tīkṣṇāṃ dhanadaḥ parighaṃ tathā .. 16 ..
5.119.d:
निस्त्रिंशं निरृतिस्तुष्ट उल्मुकं च हुताशनः ..
वायुश्च च्छुरिकां तीक्ष्णां धनदः परिघं तथा .. 16 ..
5.119.m: Nirṛti, being pleased, [gave] a sword, and the Fire-god a flaming brand; / Vāyu [gave] a sharp dagger, and the Lord of Wealth a club;

5.119.s:
daṇḍaṃ pretādhipo raudraṃ vadhāya suravidviṣām ..
dvādaśaivaṃ samālokya sā''yudhāni dvijottamāḥ .. 17 ..
5.119.d:
दण्डं प्रेताधिपो रौद्रं वधाय सुरविद्विषाम् ..
द्वादशैवं समालोक्य सा'ऽयुधानि द्विजोत्तमाः .. 17 ..
5.119.m: The lord of the departed [gave] a fierce staff for the destruction of the enemies of the gods. / Seeing these twelve weapons thus, O best of brahmins,

5.119.s:
kātyāyanī tataścakre bhujadvādaśakaṃ tadā ..
jagrāha ca drutaṃ tāni surāstrāṇi divaukasām .. 18 ..
5.119.d:
कात्यायनी ततश्चक्रे भुजद्वादशकं तदा ..
जग्राह च द्रुतं तानि सुरास्त्राणि दिवौकसाम् .. 18 ..
5.119.m: Kātyāyanī then produced twelve arms at that moment / and swiftly grasped those divine weapons of the heaven-dwellers.

5.119.s:
tataḥ provāca tānsarvānsaṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhā ..
yadarthaṃ vibudhaśreṣṭhāḥ sṛṣṭā tadbrūta mā ciram.. 19 ..
5.119.d:
ततः प्रोवाच तान्सर्वान्संप्रहृष्टतनूरुहा ..
यदर्थं विबुधश्रेष्ठाः सृष्टा तद्ब्रूत मा चिरम्.. 19 ..
5.119.m: Then, her bodily hair bristling with joy, she said to them all: / "Speak without delay, O best of gods, for what purpose I was created!

5.119.s:
sarvaṃ kāryaṃ kariṣyāmi yuṣmākaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
mahiṣo dānavo raudraḥ samutpanno'tra sāṃpratam .. 6.120.20 ..
5.119.d:
सर्वं कार्यं करिष्यामि युष्माकं नात्र संशयः ..
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
महिषो दानवो रौद्रः समुत्पन्नोऽत्र सांप्रतम् .. 6.120.20 ..
5.119.m: I will perform your entire task; there is no doubt in this." / The gods said: / "A terrible Dānava, Mahiṣa, has arisen here at this time.

5.119.s:
avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
muktvaikāṃ yoṣitaṃ tena tvamasmābhirvinirmitā .. 21 ..
5.119.d:
अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां मानुषाणां विशेषतः ..
मुक्त्वैकां योषितं तेन त्वमस्माभिर्विनिर्मिता .. 21 ..
5.119.m: He cannot be slain by all living beings, especially by men; / except for a single woman. For that reason you were created by us.

5.119.s:
tasmāttvaṃ sāṃprataṃ gaccha viṃdhyākhyaṃ parvatottamam ..
tapastatra kuruṣvogra tejo yenābhivardhate .. 22 ..
5.119.d:
तस्मात्त्वं सांप्रतं गच्छ विंध्याख्यं पर्वतोत्तमम् ..
तपस्तत्र कुरुष्वोग्र तेजो येनाभिवर्धते .. 22 ..
5.119.m: Therefore, go now to the excellent mountain named Vindhya; / perform fierce austerity there so that your radiance may increase.

5.119.s:
tatastu tejaḥsaṃyuktāṃ tvāṃ jñātvā vayameva hi ..
agre dhṛtvā kariṣyāmo yuddhaṃ tena durātmanā .. 23 ..
5.119.d:
ततस्तु तेजःसंयुक्तां त्वां ज्ञात्वा वयमेव हि ..
अग्रे धृत्वा करिष्यामो युद्धं तेन दुरात्मना .. 23 ..
5.119.m: Then, knowing you to be endowed with radiance, we ourselves / will place you in front and wage battle against that evil-minded one.

5.119.s:
tatastvacchastranirdagdhaḥ paṃcatvaṃ sa prayāsyati ..
vayaṃ ca tridaśaiśvaryaṃ labhiṣyāmo hatadviṣaḥ .. 24 ..
5.119.d:
ततस्त्वच्छस्त्रनिर्दग्धः पंचत्वं स प्रयास्यति ..
वयं च त्रिदशैश्वर्यं लभिष्यामो हतद्विषः .. 24 ..
5.119.m: Then, consumed by your weapons, he will meet his death, / and, having slain our enemy, we shall obtain the sovereignty of the gods."

5.119.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye kātyāyanyutpattivarṇanaṃnāma viṃśatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ.. ..120... .. cha ..
5.119.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये कात्यायन्युत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम विंशत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः.. ..120... .. छ ..
5.119.m: Thus ends the one hundred and twentieth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Origin of Kātyāyanī,' in the glorification of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

5.120.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
devānāṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā tataḥ sā parameśvarī ..
provāca vāhanaṃ kiṃciddevā yacchatu me drutam .....
tataḥ siṃhaṃ dadau gaurī yānārthaṃ vikṛtānanam ..
tamāruhya pratasthe sā tato viṃdhyaṃ nagaṃ prati .. 2 ..
5.120.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
देवानां तद्वचः श्रुत्वा ततः सा परमेश्वरी ..
प्रोवाच वाहनं किंचिद्देवा यच्छतु मे द्रुतम् .....
ततः सिंहं ददौ गौरी यानार्थं विकृताननम् ..
तमारुह्य प्रतस्थे सा ततो विंध्यं नगं प्रति .. 2 ..
5.120.m: Sūta said: / Hearing those words of the gods, that Supreme Goddess / then said: "Let the gods quickly grant me a mount!" / Then Gaurī gave a lion with a fierce mouth to serve as a vehicle. / Mounting it, she then set out toward the Vindhya mountain.

5.120.s:
tasyaikaṃ śṛṃgamāsthāya ramyaṃ śreṣṭhadrumānvitam ..
phalapuṣpasamākīrṇaṃ latāmaṃḍapamaṃḍitam .. 3 ..
5.120.d:
तस्यैकं शृंगमास्थाय रम्यं श्रेष्ठद्रुमान्वितम् ..
फलपुष्पसमाकीर्णं लतामंडपमंडितम् .. 3 ..
5.120.m: Taking her place on a delightful peak of it, furnished with excellent trees, / strewn with fruits and flowers, and adorned with bowers of creepers,

5.120.s:
tatastapo'karotsādhvī tīvravrataparāyaṇā ..
saṃyamyendriyavargaṃ svaṃ dhyāyamānā maheśvaram .. 4 ..
5.120.d:
ततस्तपोऽकरोत्साध्वी तीव्रव्रतपरायणा ..
संयम्येन्द्रियवर्गं स्वं ध्यायमाना महेश्वरम् .. 4 ..
5.120.m: the virtuous lady then performed austerity, dedicated to severe vows, / restraining her organs of sense, meditating upon Maheśvara.

5.120.s:
yathāyathā tapovṛddhistasyāḥ sañjāyate dvijāḥ ..
tathā rūpaṃ ca kāṃtiśca śarīre prativardhate.. 5 ..
5.120.d:
यथायथा तपोवृद्धिस्तस्याः सञ्जायते द्विजाः ..
तथा रूपं च कांतिश्च शरीरे प्रतिवर्धते.. 5 ..
5.120.m: In proportion as the increase of her austerity took place, O brahmins, / in that same measure beauty and luster increased upon her body.

5.120.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāptāstatra daityeśakiṃkarāḥ ..
te tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vratopetāmatyadbhutavapurdha rām ..
gatvā procuḥ svanāthasya mahiṣasya durātmanaḥ .. 6 ..
5.120.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तास्तत्र दैत्येशकिंकराः ..
ते तां दृष्ट्वा व्रतोपेतामत्यद्भुतवपुर्ध राम् ..
गत्वा प्रोचुः स्वनाथस्य महिषस्य दुरात्मनः .. 6 ..
5.120.m: In the meantime, the servants of the lord of the Daityas arrived there. / Seeing her devoted to vows and possessed of an exceedingly wondrous form, / they went and spoke to their lord, the evil-minded Mahiṣa.

5.120.s:
.. cārā ūcuḥ .. ..
bhramamāṇairdharāpṛṣṭhe dṛṣṭā'pūrvā kumārikā ..
vindhyācale'dya cāsmābhirbhujairdvādaśabhiryutā ..
nānāśastradharairdīptaiścarmacchāditagātrakā ..7..
5.120.d:
.. चारा ऊचुः .. ..
भ्रममाणैर्धरापृष्ठे दृष्टाऽपूर्वा कुमारिका ..
विन्ध्याचलेऽद्य चास्माभिर्भुजैर्द्वादशभिर्युता ..
नानाशस्त्रधरैर्दीप्तैश्चर्मच्छादितगात्रका ..7..
5.120.m:
The spies said:
"While wandering upon the surface of the earth, an unprecedented maiden was seen / by us today upon Mount Vindhya, endowed with twelve arms, / bearing various radiant weapons, her limbs covered in hide.

5.120.s:
na devī na ca gandharvī nāsurī nāgakanyakā ..
tādṛgrūpā purā'smābhiḥ kāciddṛṣṭā nitambinī. .. 8 ..
5.120.d:
न देवी न च गन्धर्वी नासुरी नागकन्यका ..
तादृग्रूपा पुराऽस्माभिः काचिद्दृष्टा नितम्बिनी. .. 8 ..
5.120.m: Neither goddess, nor Gandharva woman, nor Asura woman, nor Nāga maiden— / never before has such a fair-hipped woman been seen by us.

5.120.s:
na vidmo yannimittaṃ sā tapaścakre yaśasvinī ..
svargakāmā'rthakāmā vā patikāmātha vā vibho.. 9 ..
5.120.d:
न विद्मो यन्निमित्तं सा तपश्चक्रे यशस्विनी ..
स्वर्गकामाऽर्थकामा वा पतिकामाथ वा विभो.. 9 ..
5.120.m: We do not know for what purpose that glorious maiden performs austerity— / whether desiring heaven, desiring wealth, or desiring a husband, O lord."

5.120.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā mahiṣo dānavādhipaḥ ..
kāmadeva vaśaṃ prāptaḥ śravaṇādapi tatkṣaṇāt .. 6.121.10 ..
5.120.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा महिषो दानवाधिपः ..
कामदेव वशं प्राप्तः श्रवणादपि तत्क्षणात् .. 6.121.10 ..
5.120.m:
Sūta said:
Hearing their words, Mahiṣa, the lord of the Dānavas, / fell under the power of Kāmadeva the very moment he heard them.

5.120.s:
tatastānagrataḥ kṛtvā sainyena mahatā nvitaḥ ..
jagāma kautukāviṣṭo yatrāste sā tu kanyakā .. 11 ..
5.120.d:
ततस्तानग्रतः कृत्वा सैन्येन महता न्वितः ..
जगाम कौतुकाविष्टो यत्रास्ते सा तु कन्यका .. 11 ..
5.120.m: Then, placing them in front and accompanied by a great army, / filled with curiosity, he went to where the maiden was staying.

5.120.s:
yathā mṛtyukṛte mandaḥ śṛgālaḥ siṃhavallabhām ..
vane suptāṃ suviśvastāṃ sarvathāpya kutobhayām..12..
5.120.d:
यथा मृत्युकृते मन्दः शृगालः सिंहवल्लभाम् ..
वने सुप्तां सुविश्वस्तां सर्वथाप्य कुतोभयाम्..12..
5.120.m: Just as a foolish jackal, destined for death, [approaches] the beloved lioness / who is asleep in the forest, deeply trusting and utterly free from fear,

5.120.s:
tasyāḥ saṃdarśanādeva tataḥ kāmaśarairhataḥ..
sa dānavapradhānaśca tatkṣaṇādeva saddvijāḥ..13..
5.120.d:
तस्याः संदर्शनादेव ततः कामशरैर्हतः..
स दानवप्रधानश्च तत्क्षणादेव सद्द्विजाः..13..
5.120.m: so that chief of the Dānavas, struck by Kāma's arrows at the very sight of her, / [acted] in that very moment, O good brahmins.

5.120.s:
atha prāha priyaṃ vākyamekākī tatpuraḥsthitaḥ..
dhṛtvā dūrataresainyaṃ tasyā rūpeṇa mohitaḥ..14..
5.120.d:
अथ प्राह प्रियं वाक्यमेकाकी तत्पुरःस्थितः..
धृत्वा दूरतरेसैन्यं तस्या रूपेण मोहितः..14..
5.120.m: Then, keeping his army at a great distance, enamoured by her beauty, / he stood before her alone and spoke pleasant words:

5.120.s:
viruddhaṃ yauvanasyaitadvrataṃ te cāruhāsini.
tasmādetatparityaktvā trailokyasvāminī bhava .. 15 ..
5.120.d:
विरुद्धं यौवनस्यैतद्व्रतं ते चारुहासिनि.
तस्मादेतत्परित्यक्त्वा त्रैलोक्यस्वामिनी भव .. 15 ..
5.120.m: "This vow is contrary to your youth, O lady of sweet smiles. / Therefore abandon it and become the sovereign of the three worlds.

5.120.s:
ahaṃ hi mahiṣo nāma dānavendro yadi śrutaḥ ..
mayā yena sahasrākṣo dvandvayuddhe vinirjitaḥ .. 16 ..
trelokyaṃ sakalaṃ mahyaṃ sāṃprataṃ ca vaśe sthitam ..
tasmāttvaṃ bhava suśroṇi bhāryā mama suvallabhā ...7..
sahasraṃ mama bhāryāṇāmanyadasti suśobhanam..
tatsarvaṃ te'dya bhṛtyatvaṃ sāṃprataṃ praka riṣyati...8..
ahaṃ cāpi tavātyaṃtaṃ dāsabhāvaṃ samāśritaḥ..
vartayiṣyāmi suśroṇi pradattvā'śeṣasaṃpadaḥ...9..
..sūta uvāca ....
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tataḥ sā parameśvarī ..
provāca bhartsamānā taṃ kopasaṃraktalocanā..6.121.2...
dhigdhikpāpasamācāra kumāravratadhāriṇīm ..
kāmopahatacittātmā kiṃ māmitthaṃ prabhā ṣase ..2...
5.120.d:
अहं हि महिषो नाम दानवेन्द्रो यदि श्रुतः ..
मया येन सहस्राक्षो द्वन्द्वयुद्धे विनिर्जितः .. 16 ..
त्रेलोक्यं सकलं मह्यं सांप्रतं च वशे स्थितम् ..
तस्मात्त्वं भव सुश्रोणि भार्या मम सुवल्लभा ...7..
सहस्रं मम भार्याणामन्यदस्ति सुशोभनम्..
तत्सर्वं तेऽद्य भृत्यत्वं सांप्रतं प्रक रिष्यति...8..
अहं चापि तवात्यंतं दासभावं समाश्रितः..
वर्तयिष्यामि सुश्रोणि प्रदत्त्वाऽशेषसंपदः...9..
..सूत उवाच ....
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ततः सा परमेश्वरी ..
प्रोवाच भर्त्समाना तं कोपसंरक्तलोचना..6.121.2...
धिग्धिक्पापसमाचार कुमारव्रतधारिणीम् ..
कामोपहतचित्तात्मा किं मामित्थं प्रभा षसे ..2...
5.120.m:
I am indeed named Mahiṣa, the lord of the Dānavas, if you have heard of me, / by whom the thousand-eyed Indra was vanquished in single combat.
The entire three worlds are now subject to my control. / Therefore, O fair-hipped lady, become my dearly beloved wife.
I have another thousand most beautiful wives; / they all shall presently become your servants today.
And I too, having assumed the role of your devoted servant, / shall serve you, O fair-hipped lady, having bestowed all my wealth upon you."
Sūta said:
Hearing his words, the supreme goddess, / rebuking him, spoke with eyes reddened with rage:
"Fie, fie, O worker of evil! To me, who observe the vow of maidenhood, / your mind stricken with desire, why do you speak thus?

5.120.s:
ahaṃ tava vadhārthāya nirmitā vibudhottamaiḥ ..
tasmāttvāṃ nāśayiṣyāmi smareṣṭaṃ yaddhṛdi sthitam..22..
5.120.d:
अहं तव वधार्थाय निर्मिता विबुधोत्तमैः ..
तस्मात्त्वां नाशयिष्यामि स्मरेष्टं यद्धृदि स्थितम्..22..
5.120.m: I was created by the foremost gods for your destruction. / Therefore I shall destroy you; remember what desire resides in your heart!"

5.120.s:
.. mahiṣa uvāca .. ..
yadyevaṃ tadvarārohe yuktā syācca kumārikā ..
prārthanīyā bhavedatra sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ yataḥ ..23..
5.120.d:
.. महिष उवाच .. ..
यद्येवं तद्वरारोहे युक्ता स्याच्च कुमारिका ..
प्रार्थनीया भवेदत्र सर्वेषां प्राणिनां यतः ..23..
5.120.m:
Mahiṣa said:
"If so, O lovely-hipped lady, a maiden would be suitable, / since she is to be wooed by all living beings in this world.

5.120.s:
svargārthaṃ kriyate dharmastapaśca varavarṇini ..
yena bhogāḥ prabhuñjaṃti ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ .. 24 ..
5.120.d:
स्वर्गार्थं क्रियते धर्मस्तपश्च वरवर्णिनि ..
येन भोगाः प्रभुञ्जंति ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः .. 24 ..
5.120.m: Dharma and austerity are performed for heaven's sake, O fair lady, / so that one may enjoy pleasures, both divine and human.

5.120.s:
tasmāddehi mamātmānaṃ gāṃdharveṇa suśobhane ..
vivāhena yato'nyeṣāṃ sa pradhānaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..25..
5.120.d:
तस्माद्देहि ममात्मानं गांधर्वेण सुशोभने ..
विवाहेन यतोऽन्येषां स प्रधानः प्रकीर्तितः ..25..
5.120.m: Therefore give yourself to me in the Gandharva / marriage, O most beautiful lady, since among others that is proclaimed paramount."

5.120.s:
evaṃ pravadatastasya sā devī krodhamūrchitā ..
tadvaktrāṃtaṃ samuddiśya śaraṃ cikṣepa sa kṣaṇāt ..26..
5.120.d:
एवं प्रवदतस्तस्य सा देवी क्रोधमूर्छिता ..
तद्वक्त्रांतं समुद्दिश्य शरं चिक्षेप स क्षणात् ..26..
5.120.m: As he spoke thus, the goddess, overwhelmed with anger, / instantly discharged an arrow aimed at his mouth.

5.120.s:
viveśa vadanaṃ tasya valmīkaṃ pannago yathā ..
atha tairmārgagaṇairviddhaḥ sa vaktrāṃtānnadaṃstataḥ ..27..
5.120.d:
विवेश वदनं तस्य वल्मीकं पन्नगो यथा ..
अथ तैर्मार्गगणैर्विद्धः स वक्त्रांतान्नदंस्ततः ..27..
5.120.m: It entered his mouth as a serpent enters an anthill. / Then, pierced in his mouth by those arrows and roaring,

5.120.s:
susrāva rudhiraṃ bhūri gairikaṃ parvato yathā ..
tataḥ kopaparītātmā nivṛttyātha śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ..28..
5.120.d:
सुस्राव रुधिरं भूरि गैरिकं पर्वतो यथा ..
ततः कोपपरीतात्मा निवृत्त्याथ शनैः शनैः ..28..
5.120.m: he poured forth abundant blood, like red ochre from a mountain. / Then, his mind overcome with rage, retreating very slowly,

5.120.s:
svasainyaṃ tvarito bheje kāmena ca vaśī kṛtaḥ..
provāca sainikānsarvānduṣṭā strīyaṃ pragṛhyatām ..
yathā na tyajati prāṇānprahārairjarjarīkṛtā..29..
5.120.d:
स्वसैन्यं त्वरितो भेजे कामेन च वशी कृतः..
प्रोवाच सैनिकान्सर्वान्दुष्टा स्त्रीयं प्रगृह्यताम् ..
यथा न त्यजति प्राणान्प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृता..29..
5.120.m: he quickly rejoined his army; yet still overcome by desire, / he said to all his soldiers: 'Let this wicked woman be seized, / so that she does not lose her life, shattered by blows.

5.120.s:
eṣā mama na sandehaḥ priyā bhāryā bhaviṣyati..
yadi no śastrapātena paṃcatvamupayāsyati .. 6.121.30 ..
evamuktāstadā tena dānavā yuddhadurmadāḥ ..
dudruvuḥ sammukhāstasyā muñcanto niśitāñcharān.3...
5.120.d:
एषा मम न सन्देहः प्रिया भार्या भविष्यति..
यदि नो शस्त्रपातेन पंचत्वमुपयास्यति .. 6.121.30 ..
एवमुक्तास्तदा तेन दानवा युद्धदुर्मदाः ..
दुद्रुवुः सम्मुखास्तस्या मुञ्चन्तो निशिताञ्छरान्.3...
5.120.m:
She will undoubtedly become my beloved wife, / if she does not go to dissolution through the fall of weapons.'
Thus commanded by him, the Dānavas, reckless in battle, / ran towards her, discharging sharp arrows.

5.120.s:
etasminnaṃtare devī sā dṛṣṭvā tānupasthitān ..
yuddhāya kṛtasaṃkalpāṃstarjataśca muhurmuhuḥ. 32 ..
5.120.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवी सा दृष्ट्वा तानुपस्थितान् ..
युद्धाय कृतसंकल्पांस्तर्जतश्च मुहुर्मुहुः. 32 ..
5.120.m: Meanwhile, the goddess, seeing them arrived, / resolved on battle and shouting threats again and again,

5.120.s:
tatastu līlayā devī muktā tīkṣṇānmahāśarān ..
tānsarvāṃstāḍayāmāsa sarvamarmasu tatkṣaṇāt .. 33 ..
5.120.d:
ततस्तु लीलया देवी मुक्ता तीक्ष्णान्महाशरान् ..
तान्सर्वांस्ताडयामास सर्वमर्मसु तत्क्षणात् .. 33 ..
5.120.m: effortlessly released sharp, mighty arrows / and struck them all in their vital points at that very instant.

5.120.s:
atha tīkṣṇaiḥ śarairdaityā nihatā dānavāstathā ..
eke paṃcatvamāpannā gatāścānya itastataḥ..34..
5.120.d:
अथ तीक्ष्णैः शरैर्दैत्या निहता दानवास्तथा ..
एके पंचत्वमापन्ना गताश्चान्य इतस्ततः..34..
5.120.m: Then, slain by the sharp arrows, the Daityas and Dānavas— / some met their death, while others scattered here and there.

5.120.s:
tataḥ sainyaṃ samālokya tadbhagnaṃ ca tayā raṇe ..
kopāviṣṭastato daityaḥ svayaṃ tāṃ samupādravat .. 35 ..
5.120.d:
ततः सैन्यं समालोक्य तद्भग्नं च तया रणे ..
कोपाविष्टस्ततो दैत्यः स्वयं तां समुपाद्रवत् .. 35 ..
5.120.m: Then, seeing his army broken by her in battle, / the Daitya, filled with rage, rushed at her himself,

5.120.s:
yacchañchṛṃgaprahārāṃśca tasyāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ ..
garjitaṃ vidadhaccograṃ śāradābhrasamaṃ muhuḥ .. 36 ..
5.120.d:
यच्छञ्छृंगप्रहारांश्च तस्याः शतसहस्रशः ..
गर्जितं विदधच्चोग्रं शारदाभ्रसमं मुहुः .. 36 ..
5.120.m: striking her hundreds and thousands of times with his horns, / repeatedly letting out fierce roars like an autumn cloud.

5.120.s:
etasminnaṃtare devī sāṭṭahāsakṛtasvanā ..
trailokyavivaraṃ sarvaṃ yacchabdena prapūritam . 37 ..
5.120.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवी साट्टहासकृतस्वना ..
त्रैलोक्यविवरं सर्वं यच्छब्देन प्रपूरितम् . 37 ..
5.120.m: Meanwhile, the goddess uttered a loud, mocking laugh / by whose sound the entire cavity of the three worlds was filled.

5.120.s:
evaṃ tasyā hasaṃtyāśca vaktrāntādatha niryayuḥ..
puliṃdāḥ śabarā mlechāstathānye'raṇyavāsinaḥ..38..
5.120.d:
एवं तस्या हसंत्याश्च वक्त्रान्तादथ निर्ययुः..
पुलिंदाः शबरा म्लेछास्तथान्येऽरण्यवासिनः..38..
5.120.m: And as she laughed thus, there came forth from her mouth / Pulindas, Śabaras, Mlecchas, and other forest dwellers,

5.120.s:
śakāśca yavanāścaiva śataśaśtu vapurdharā?..
varma sthagitagātrāśca yamadūtā ivāpare..39..
te procurdevi no brūhi yena sṛṣṭā vayaṃ kṣitau..
kāryeṇa kriyate kṛtsnaṃ yena śīghraṃ varānane..6.121.4...
5.120.d:
शकाश्च यवनाश्चैव शतशश्तु वपुर्धरा?..
वर्म स्थगितगात्राश्च यमदूता इवापरे..39..
ते प्रोचुर्देवि नो ब्रूहि येन सृष्टा वयं क्षितौ..
कार्येण क्रियते कृत्स्नं येन शीघ्रं वरानने..6.121.4...
5.120.m:
Śakas and Yavanas in their hundreds, having assumed bodily form, / their limbs clad in armour, like other messengers of Yama.
They said: "O goddess, tell us for what task we were created on earth, / so that it may be accomplished swiftly, O lovely-faced one!"

5.120.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
etānasya suduṣṭasya sainikānbalagarvitān ..
sūdayadhvaṃ drutaṃ vākyādasmadīyādyathecchayā .. 41 ..
5.120.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
एतानस्य सुदुष्टस्य सैनिकान्बलगर्वितान् ..
सूदयध्वं द्रुतं वाक्यादस्मदीयाद्यथेच्छया .. 41 ..
5.120.m:
The goddess said:
"These soldiers of that vile wretch, arrogant with might— / slaughter them swiftly at my command, as you please!"

5.120.s:
atha te tadvacaḥ śrutvā valgaṃto'sidhanurddharāḥ ..
daiteyabalamuddiśya dudruvurvegamāśritāḥ .. 42 ..
5.120.d:
अथ ते तद्वचः श्रुत्वा वल्गंतोऽसिधनुर्द्धराः ..
दैतेयबलमुद्दिश्य दुद्रुवुर्वेगमाश्रिताः .. 42 ..
5.120.m: Then, hearing her word, brandishing swords and bows, / they charged with great speed toward the Daitya host.

5.120.s:
tatasteṣāṃ mahadyuddhaṃ mitho jajñe sudāruṇam .
nātmīyaṃ na paraṃ tatra kenacijjñā yate kvacit .. 43 ..
5.120.d:
ततस्तेषां महद्युद्धं मिथो जज्ञे सुदारुणम् .
नात्मीयं न परं तत्र केनचिज्ज्ञा यते क्वचित् .. 43 ..
5.120.m: Then a great, terrible battle arose between them; / neither one's own nor the enemy could be distinguished there by anyone.

5.120.s:
atha te dānavāḥ sarve yodhairdevīsamudbhavaiḥ ..
bhagnā vyāpāditāścānye prahārairjarjarīkṛtāḥ .. 44 ..
5.120.d:
अथ ते दानवाः सर्वे योधैर्देवीसमुद्भवैः ..
भग्ना व्यापादिताश्चान्ये प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृताः .. 44 ..
5.120.m: Then all those Dānavas were broken by the warriors born of the goddess, / and others were slaughtered, shattered by blows.

5.120.s:
tato bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahiṣaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ ..
tāmuvāca krudhā devīṃ vacanaiḥ paruṣākṣaraiḥ .. 45 ..
5.120.d:
ततो भग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा महिषः क्रोधमूर्छितः ..
तामुवाच क्रुधा देवीं वचनैः परुषाक्षरैः .. 45 ..
5.120.m: Seeing his army broken, Mahiṣa, frantic with rage, / angrily spoke to the goddess with harsh words:

5.120.s:
āḥ pāpe strīti matvādya na hatāsi mayā yudhi ..
tasmātpaśya prahāraṃ me tattvaṃ budhyasi nānyathā .. 46 ..
5.120.d:
आः पापे स्त्रीति मत्वाद्य न हतासि मया युधि ..
तस्मात्पश्य प्रहारं मे तत्त्वं बुध्यसि नान्यथा .. 46 ..
5.120.m: "Ah, wicked one! Thinking you a woman, you were not killed by me in battle today. / Therefore behold my strike! You will learn the truth, not otherwise!"

5.120.s:
evamuktvā viśeṣeṇa prahārānsa vicikṣipe ..
viṣāṇābhyāṃ mahāvego bhartsayāno muhurmuhuḥ .. 47 ..
5.120.d:
एवमुक्त्वा विशेषेण प्रहारान्स विचिक्षिपे ..
विषाणाभ्यां महावेगो भर्त्सयानो मुहुर्मुहुः .. 47 ..
5.120.m: Having spoken thus, he furiously dealt blows / with both horns at great speed, threatening her again and again.

5.120.s:
tato'bhyāśagataṃ dṛṣṭvā sā devī dānavaṃ ca tam ..
ārurohātha vegena pṛṣṭhideśena kopataḥ .. 48 ..
5.120.d:
ततोऽभ्याशगतं दृष्ट्वा सा देवी दानवं च तम् ..
आरुरोहाथ वेगेन पृष्ठिदेशेन कोपतः .. 48 ..
5.120.m: Then, seeing that Dānava come near, the goddess / swiftly leaped in anger upon his back.

5.120.s:
tataścukrośa daityo'sau vyomamārgaṃ samāśritaḥ ..
pṛṣṭhyāstalena nirbhinno rudhiraughapariplutaḥ .. 49 ..
5.120.d:
ततश्चुक्रोश दैत्योऽसौ व्योममार्गं समाश्रितः ..
पृष्ठ्यास्तलेन निर्भिन्नो रुधिरौघपरिप्लुतः .. 49 ..
5.120.m: Then that Daitya, taking to the path of the sky, screamed, / pierced through the sole [of her foot] upon his back and drenched in streams of blood.

5.120.s:
etasminnaṃtare siṃhaḥ sa tasyā jyotisaṃbhavaḥ ..
jagrāha paścime bhāge daṃṣṭrāgrairniśitaiḥ krudhā .. 6.121.50 ..
5.120.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे सिंहः स तस्या ज्योतिसंभवः ..
जग्राह पश्चिमे भागे दंष्ट्राग्रैर्निशितैः क्रुधा .. 6.121.50 ..
5.120.m: Meanwhile, her lion, born of light, / seized him furiously by the hindquarters with the tips of his sharp fangs.

5.120.s:
tato niścalatāṃ prāptaḥ pādākrāṃtaśca dānavaḥ..
akarodbhairavānnādānna śaktaścalituṃ padam .. 51 ..
5.120.d:
ततो निश्चलतां प्राप्तः पादाक्रांतश्च दानवः..
अकरोद्भैरवान्नादान्न शक्तश्चलितुं पदम् .. 51 ..
5.120.m: Then, rendered immobile and pinned down by her foot, the Dānava / uttered terrible cries, unable to move a single step.

5.120.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāptāḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ..
vyomasthāstāṃ tadā procurdevīṃ harṣasamanvitāḥ .. 52 ..
5.120.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्ताः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ..
व्योमस्थास्तां तदा प्रोचुर्देवीं हर्षसमन्विताः .. 52 ..
5.120.m: At that moment, all the gods along with Indra arrived; / standing in the sky, filled with joy, they then said to the goddess:

5.120.s:
etasya śirasaśchedaṃ śīghraṃ kuru sureśvari ..
khaṅgenānena tīkṣṇena yāvanno yāti cānyataḥ .. 53 ..
5.120.d:
एतस्य शिरसश्छेदं शीघ्रं कुरु सुरेश्वरि ..
खङ्गेनानेन तीक्ष्णेन यावन्नो याति चान्यतः .. 53 ..
5.120.m: "O ruler of the gods, quickly cut off his head / with this sharp sword, before he goes elsewhere!"

5.120.s:
sā śrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ devī kopasamanvitā ..
khaḍgaṃ vyāpārayāmāsa kaṃṭhe tasyātipīvare .. 54 ..
5.120.d:
सा श्रुत्वा वचनं तेषां देवी कोपसमन्विता ..
खड्गं व्यापारयामास कंठे तस्यातिपीवरे .. 54 ..
5.120.m: Hearing their words, the goddess, filled with rage, / applied the sword to his massive throat.

5.120.s:
sa tena khaḍgaghātena kaṃṭhaḥ pīno'pi niṣṭhuraḥ..
dvidhā jajñe'tha daityasya dadhattuṣṭiṃ divaukasām .. 55 ..
5.120.d:
स तेन खड्गघातेन कंठः पीनोऽपि निष्ठुरः..
द्विधा जज्ञेऽथ दैत्यस्य दधत्तुष्टिं दिवौकसाम् .. 55 ..
5.120.m: By that sword-stroke, the Daitya's throat, though thick and hard, / was cleaved in two, bringing satisfaction to the gods.

5.120.s:
dvādaśārkapratīkāśo vaktrāṃtaścarmakhaḍgadhṛk ..
bhartsayaṃstāṃ mahādevīṃ khaḍgodyatakarāṃ tadā ..
khaḍgaṃ vyāpārayangātre tasyā bālārkasannibham .. 56 ..
5.120.d:
द्वादशार्कप्रतीकाशो वक्त्रांतश्चर्मखड्गधृक् ..
भर्त्सयंस्तां महादेवीं खड्गोद्यतकरां तदा ..
खड्गं व्यापारयन्गात्रे तस्या बालार्कसन्निभम् .. 56 ..
5.120.m: Resembling twelve suns, emerging from the mouth, holding a shield and sword, / threatening the great goddess whose hand was raised with the sword, / he then swung his sword, which resembled the morning sun, at her body.

5.120.s:
tataḥ keśeṣu cādhāya yāvattasyāpi cikṣipe .
prahāraṃ gātranāśāya tāvadūce sa dānavaḥ .. 57 ..
5.120.d:
ततः केशेषु चाधाय यावत्तस्यापि चिक्षिपे .
प्रहारं गात्रनाशाय तावदूचे स दानवः .. 57 ..
5.120.m: Then, seizing him by the hair, as she struck [him] / to destroy his body, the Dānava spoke:

5.120.s:
.. dānava uvāca .. ..
jaya devi jayāciṃtye jaya sarvasureśvari ..
jaya sarvagate devi jaya sarvajanapriye .. 58 ..
5.120.d:
.. दानव उवाच .. ..
जय देवि जयाचिंत्ये जय सर्वसुरेश्वरि ..
जय सर्वगते देवि जय सर्वजनप्रिये .. 58 ..
5.120.m: The Dānava said: / "Victory, O goddess! Victory, O inconceivable one! Victory, O ruler of all the gods! / Victory, O all-pervading goddess! Victory, O beloved of all beings!

5.120.s:
jaya kāmaprade nityaṃ jaya trailokyasundari ..
jaya trailokya rakṣārthamudyate hyakutobhaye .. 59 ..
5.120.d:
जय कामप्रदे नित्यं जय त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरि ..
जय त्रैलोक्य रक्षार्थमुद्यते ह्यकुतोभये .. 59 ..
5.120.m: Victory, O eternal giver of desires! Victory, O beauty of the three worlds! / Victory, O fearless one, intent upon protecting the three worlds!

5.120.s:
jaya devi kṛtānaṃde jaya daityavināśini ..
jaya kleśacchide kāṃte jayābhaktavimohade .. 6.121.60 ..
tvaṃ sṛṣṭistvaṃ varā devī tvaṃ lakṣmīstvaṃ sarasvatī .
tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ..6...
5.120.d:
जय देवि कृतानंदे जय दैत्यविनाशिनि ..
जय क्लेशच्छिदे कांते जयाभक्तविमोहदे .. 6.121.60 ..
त्वं सृष्टिस्त्वं वरा देवी त्वं लक्ष्मीस्त्वं सरस्वती .
त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा तुष्टिः पुष्टिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ..6...
5.120.m:
Victory, O joyful goddess! Victory, O destroyer of Daityas! / Victory, O destroyer of distress, O lovely one! Victory, O deluder of the non-devoted!
You are creation, you are the supreme goddess, you are Lakṣmī, you are Sarasvatī, / you are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, contentment, nourishment, intellect, firmness, forgiveness.

5.120.s:
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me prāṇānrakṣa dayāṃ kuru..
praṇatasya sudīnasya hīnasya ca viśeṣataḥ..62..
5.120.d:
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं मे प्राणान्रक्ष दयां कुरु..
प्रणतस्य सुदीनस्य हीनस्य च विशेषतः..62..
5.120.m: Therefore grant me your favor, preserve my life, have mercy / upon one who bows down, who is very wretched, and especially humbled.

5.120.s:
ahaṃ durvāsasā śapto hiraṇyākṣasuto balī..
mahiṣatvaṃ samānītastvayā devī vimokṣitaḥ..63..
5.120.d:
अहं दुर्वाससा शप्तो हिरण्याक्षसुतो बली..
महिषत्वं समानीतस्त्वया देवी विमोक्षितः..63..
5.120.m: I am the mighty son of Hiraṇyākṣa, cursed by Durvāsas / and brought to the state of a buffalo; by you, O goddess, I have been liberated.

5.120.s:
tasmāddarpaḥ pramukto'dya mayā dānavasaṃbhavaḥ..
kiṃkaratvaṃ prayāsyāmi sāṃprataṃ te sureśvari..64..
5.120.d:
तस्माद्दर्पः प्रमुक्तोऽद्य मया दानवसंभवः..
किंकरत्वं प्रयास्यामि सांप्रतं ते सुरेश्वरि..64..
5.120.m: Therefore my pride born of the Dānavas has been abandoned today; / I will henceforth become your servant, O ruler of the gods!

5.120.s: jaya sarvagate devi sarvaduṣṭavināśini..65..
5.120.d: जय सर्वगते देवि सर्वदुष्टविनाशिनि..65..
5.120.m: Victory, O all-pervading goddess, destroyer of all wicked ones!"

5.120.s:
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā kṛpaṇaṃ sā sureśvarī ..
kṛpāviṣṭā'bravīdvākyaṃ tato vyomasthitānsurān..66..
5.120.d:
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कृपणं सा सुरेश्वरी ..
कृपाविष्टाऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं ततो व्योमस्थितान्सुरान्..66..
5.120.m: Hearing his pathetic plea, that ruler of the gods, / moved by compassion, then spoke these words to the gods standing in the sky:

5.120.s:
kiṃ karomi dayā jātā mamainaṃ prati he surāḥ ..
tasmānnāhaṃ haniṣyāmi dānavaṃ dīnajalpakam .. 67 ..
5.120.d:
किं करोमि दया जाता ममैनं प्रति हे सुराः ..
तस्मान्नाहं हनिष्यामि दानवं दीनजल्पकम् .. 67 ..
5.120.m: "What shall I do? Compassion for him has arisen in me, O gods; / therefore I will not slay this Dānava who speaks so piteously.

5.120.s:
vimukhaṃ khaḍgaśastraṃ ca tavāsmīti pravādinam ..
api me pitṛhaṃtāraṃ na hanyāṃ ripumāhave .. 68 ..
5.120.d:
विमुखं खड्गशस्त्रं च तवास्मीति प्रवादिनम् ..
अपि मे पितृहंतारं न हन्यां रिपुमाहवे .. 68 ..
5.120.m: Even if an enemy were the killer of my father, I would not strike him in battle / if he has turned away his face, laid down his sword and weapon, and says, 'I am yours.'"

5.120.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. .
na cedasi ca deveśi tvamenaṃ dānavādhamam ..
nāśayiṣyati tatkṛtsnaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 69 ..
5.120.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. .
न चेदसि च देवेशि त्वमेनं दानवाधमम् ..
नाशयिष्यति तत्कृत्स्नं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् .. 69 ..
5.120.m: The gods said: / "O ruler of the gods, if you do not slay this lowest of Dānavas, / he will destroy the entire three worlds with all that moves and is still.

5.120.s:
eṣa vyarthaḥśramaḥ sarvastathāsmākaṃ bhaviṣyati ..
tava saṃbhūtisaṃbhūtastava kleśastathā'khilaḥ .. 6.121.70 ..
5.120.d:
एष व्यर्थःश्रमः सर्वस्तथास्माकं भविष्यति ..
तव संभूतिसंभूतस्तव क्लेशस्तथाऽखिलः .. 6.121.70 ..
5.120.m: All our labor will thus be in vain, / as will the trouble born of your manifestation, and your entire exertion."

5.120.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
nāhamenaṃ haniṣyāmi tyajiṣyāmi tathā'marāḥ ..
enaṃ kacagrahaṃ kṛtvā dhārayiṣyāmi sarvadā .. 71 ..
5.120.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
नाहमेनं हनिष्यामि त्यजिष्यामि तथाऽमराः ..
एनं कचग्रहं कृत्वा धारयिष्यामि सर्वदा .. 71 ..
5.120.m: The goddess said: / "I shall not kill him, nor shall I let him go, O immortals; / grasping him by the hair, I shall hold him always."

5.120.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
sādhusādhu mahābhāge yuktamuktaṃ tvayā vacaḥ ..
etaddhi yujyate kartuṃ kāle'smiṃstridaśeśvari .. 72 ..
5.120.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
साधुसाधु महाभागे युक्तमुक्तं त्वया वचः ..
एतद्धि युज्यते कर्तुं कालेऽस्मिंस्त्रिदशेश्वरि .. 72 ..
5.120.m: The gods said: / "Well done, well done, O highly fortunate one! You have spoken fitting words; / this indeed is proper to do at this time, O ruler of the thirty [gods]!

5.120.s:
sāṃprataṃ martyaloke tvaṃ rūpametatsamāśritā ..
śastrodyatakarā raudrā mahiṣopari saṃsthitā .. 73 ..
5.120.d:
सांप्रतं मर्त्यलोके त्वं रूपमेतत्समाश्रिता ..
शस्त्रोद्यतकरा रौद्रा महिषोपरि संस्थिता .. 73 ..
5.120.m: Now, assuming this form in the mortal realm— / terrifying, with weapon raised in hand, standing atop the buffalo—

5.120.s:
avāpsyasi parāṃ pūjāṃ durlabhā mamarairapi ..
yastvāmetena rūpeṇa saṃsthitāṃ pūjayiṣyati .. 74 ..
5.120.d:
अवाप्स्यसि परां पूजां दुर्लभा ममरैरपि ..
यस्त्वामेतेन रूपेण संस्थितां पूजयिष्यति .. 74 ..
5.120.m: you will receive supreme worship, difficult even for the immortals to obtain. / Whoever worships you standing in this form—

5.120.s:
tvamasya saṃgato bhāvi vikhyātā viṃdhyavāsinī ..
kiṃ te vā bahunoktena śṛṇu saṃkṣepato vacaḥ .. 75 ..
5.120.d:
त्वमस्य संगतो भावि विख्याता विंध्यवासिनी ..
किं ते वा बहुनोक्तेन शृणु संक्षेपतो वचः .. 75 ..
5.120.m: united with him, you will become renowned as Vindhyavāsinī. / What need is there of saying much to you? Hear our words in brief:

5.120.s:
asmadīyaṃ paraṃ tathyaṃ sarvalokahitāvaham ..
pārthivānāṃ tvadāyattaṃ balaṃ devi bhaviṣyati .. 76 ..
5.120.d:
अस्मदीयं परं तथ्यं सर्वलोकहितावहम् ..
पार्थिवानां त्वदायत्तं बलं देवि भविष्यति .. 76 ..
5.120.m: Our supreme truth brings welfare to all worlds: / the strength of earthly kings shall be dependent on you, O goddess,

5.120.s:
yuddhakāle samutpanne bhaktānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
prasthānaṃ vā praveśaṃ ca yaḥ kariṣyati mānavaḥ .. 77 ..
5.120.d:
युद्धकाले समुत्पन्ने भक्तानां नात्र संशयः ..
प्रस्थानं वा प्रवेशं च यः करिष्यति मानवः .. 77 ..
5.120.m: when the time of battle arises for your devotees—of this there is no doubt. / Whatever person undertakes a departure or an entrance

5.120.s:
tvāṃ smṛtvā praṇipatyātha pūjayitvā viśeṣataḥ ..
tasya saṃpatsyate siddhiḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā ..
iha kāpuruṣasyāpi kiṃ punaḥ subhaṭasya ca .. 78 ..
5.120.d:
त्वां स्मृत्वा प्रणिपत्याथ पूजयित्वा विशेषतः ..
तस्य संपत्स्यते सिद्धिः सर्वकृत्येषु सर्वदा ..
इह कापुरुषस्यापि किं पुनः सुभटस्य च .. 78 ..
5.120.m: having remembered you, bowed down, and especially worshipped you, / success will be accomplished for him in all tasks at all times; / even for a coward in this world, let alone for a valiant warrior!

5.120.s:
āśvinasya site pakṣe navamyāṃ cāṣṭamīdine ..
pūjayiṣyati yo marttyastvāṃ sadbhaktisamanvitaḥ .. 79 ..
5.120.d:
आश्विनस्य सिते पक्षे नवम्यां चाष्टमीदिने ..
पूजयिष्यति यो मर्त्त्यस्त्वां सद्भक्तिसमन्वितः .. 79 ..
5.120.m: Whatever mortal worships you with true devotion / in the bright fortnight of Āśvina on the ninth and the eighth day,

5.120.s:
tasya saṃvatsaraṃ yāvatsamagraṃ surasundari ..
na bhaviṣyati vai rogo na bhayaṃ na parābhavaḥ ..
nāpamṛtyurna caurādi samudbhūta upadravaḥ .. 6.121.80 ..
5.120.d:
तस्य संवत्सरं यावत्समग्रं सुरसुन्दरि ..
न भविष्यति वै रोगो न भयं न पराभवः ..
नापमृत्युर्न चौरादि समुद्भूत उपद्रवः .. 6.121.80 ..
5.120.m: for him, O beautiful one of the gods, for an entire full year / there will be no illness, no fear, no defeat, / no untimely death, and no affliction arising from thieves and the like."

5.120.s:
. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvātha te devāstāṃ devīṃ harṣasaṃyutāḥ ..
anujñātāstayā jagmuḥ svāṃ purīmamarāvatīm .. .. 91 ..
tatra gatvā cirātprāpya svaṃ rājyaṃ pākaśāsanaḥ ..
pālayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭastrailokyaṃ hatakaṭakam .. 82 ..
lokāśca sukhasaṃpannāḥ sarve jātā stataḥ param..
yajñabhāgabhujo devā bhūyo jātā jagattraye .. 83 ..
tataḥ paraṃ ca sā devī trailokye khyātimāgatā ..
sarvakṣetreṣu tīrtheṣu sthāneṣu ca viśeṣataḥ .. 84 ..
etasminnaṃtare jātaḥ surathonāma bhūpatiḥ ..
ānartastena sadbhaktyā kṣetre'traiva vinirmitā .. 85 ..
yastāṃ paśyati sadbhaktyā caitrāṣṭamyāṃ site'hani ..
sa pumānvatsaraṃ yāvatkṛtārthaḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ .. 86 ..
5.120.d:
. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वाथ ते देवास्तां देवीं हर्षसंयुताः ..
अनुज्ञातास्तया जग्मुः स्वां पुरीममरावतीम् .. .. 91 ..
तत्र गत्वा चिरात्प्राप्य स्वं राज्यं पाकशासनः ..
पालयामास संहृष्टस्त्रैलोक्यं हतकटकम् .. 82 ..
लोकाश्च सुखसंपन्नाः सर्वे जाता स्ततः परम्..
यज्ञभागभुजो देवा भूयो जाता जगत्त्रये .. 83 ..
ततः परं च सा देवी त्रैलोक्ये ख्यातिमागता ..
सर्वक्षेत्रेषु तीर्थेषु स्थानेषु च विशेषतः .. 84 ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे जातः सुरथोनाम भूपतिः ..
आनर्तस्तेन सद्भक्त्या क्षेत्रेऽत्रैव विनिर्मिता .. 85 ..
यस्तां पश्यति सद्भक्त्या चैत्राष्टम्यां सितेऽहनि ..
स पुमान्वत्सरं यावत्कृतार्थः स्यान्न संशयः .. 86 ..
5.120.m:
Sūta said: / Having spoken thus to that goddess, those gods, filled with joy, / permitted by her, went to their own city, Amarāvatī.
Going there, having regained his kingdom after a long time, Indra, / delighted, protected the three worlds from which hostile forces had been destroyed.
And after that, all the worlds became endowed with happiness; / the gods once again became enjoyers of sacrificial shares in the three worlds.
And after that, that goddess attained fame in the three worlds, / especially in all sacred fields, sacred fords, and holy shrines.
Meanwhile, a king named Suratha was born / in Ānarta; by him, with true devotion, [an image of her] was fashioned right in this sacred field.
Whoever beholds her with true devotion on the bright eighth day of Caitra, / that man will have his purpose achieved for a year, there is no doubt.

5.120.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye mahiṣāsuraparājaya kātyāyanīmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma ekaviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 121 .. .. ..
5.120.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये महिषासुरपराजय कात्यायनीमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम एकविंशत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 121 .. .. ..
5.120.m: Thus ends the one hundred twenty-first chapter, named 'Defeat of Mahiṣāsura and Description of the Glory of Kātyāyanī,' in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya of the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.121.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭosmi dvijottamāḥ ..
yathā sa nihato devyā mahiṣākhyo danūttamaḥ .. 1 ..
5.121.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टोस्मि द्विजोत्तमाः ..
यथा स निहतो देव्या महिषाख्यो दनूत्तमः .. 1 ..
5.121.m: Sūta said: / All this has been narrated to you, as I was asked, O best of the twice-born, / how that best of Danu's sons, named Mahiṣa, was slain by the goddess.

5.121.s:
sāṃprataṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāṃ pātakanāśinīm ..
kedārasaṃbhavāṃ puṇyāṃ tāṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ samāhitāḥ .. 2 ..
5.121.d:
सांप्रतं कीर्तयिष्यामि कथां पातकनाशिनीम् ..
केदारसंभवां पुण्यां तां शृणुध्वं समाहिताः .. 2 ..
5.121.m: Now I shall recite the meritorious story born of Kedāra, / which destroys sins; listen to it attentively!

5.121.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. .
kedāraḥ śrūyate sūta gaṃgādvāre himācale ..
sa kathaṃ ceha saṃprāptaḥ sarvaṃ vistarato vada .. 3 ..
5.121.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. .
केदारः श्रूयते सूत गंगाद्वारे हिमाचले ..
स कथं चेह संप्राप्तः सर्वं विस्तरतो वद .. 3 ..
5.121.m:
The seers said:
Kedāra is heard of, O Sūta, at Gaṅgādvāra in the Himālayas.
How did he arrive here? Tell [us] everything in full detail.

5.121.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etatsatyaṃ girau tasminsvayaṃbhūḥ saṃsthitaḥ prabhuḥ ..
paraṃ tatra vaseddevo yāvanmāsāṣṭakaṃ dvijāḥ .. 4 .
5.121.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतत्सत्यं गिरौ तस्मिन्स्वयंभूः संस्थितः प्रभुः ..
परं तत्र वसेद्देवो यावन्मासाष्टकं द्विजाः .. 4 .
5.121.m:
Sūta said:
This is true: upon that mountain the Lord is present, self-manifest.
However, the god resides there for eight months, O brahmins.

5.121.s:
yāvadgharmaśca varṣā ca tāvattatra vasetprabhuḥ ..
śītakāle punaścātra kṣetre saṃtiṣṭhate sadā .. .. 5 ..
5.121.d:
यावद्घर्मश्च वर्षा च तावत्तत्र वसेत्प्रभुः ..
शीतकाले पुनश्चात्र क्षेत्रे संतिष्ठते सदा .. .. 5 ..
5.121.m:
As long as there is summer and the rainy season, so long does the Lord reside there;
and in the cold season, he always remains here in this sacred field.

5.121.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kiṃ tatkāryaṃ vasedyena kṣetre māsacatuṣṭayam ..
himācale yathaivāṣṭau sūtaputra vadasva naḥ .. 6 ..
5.121.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
किं तत्कार्यं वसेद्येन क्षेत्रे मासचतुष्टयम् ..
हिमाचले यथैवाष्टौ सूतपुत्र वदस्व नः .. 6 ..
5.121.m:
The seers said:
What is that purpose for which he resides in this sacred field for four months,
just as [he stays] eight in the Himālayas? Tell us, O son of Sūta.

5.121.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
pūrvaṃ svāyaṃbhuvasyādau manordaityo mahābalaḥ ..
hiraṇyākṣo mahātejāstapovīryasamanvitaḥ .. 7 ..
5.121.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
पूर्वं स्वायंभुवस्यादौ मनोर्दैत्यो महाबलः ..
हिरण्याक्षो महातेजास्तपोवीर्यसमन्वितः .. 7 ..
5.121.m:
Sūta said:
Long ago, at the beginning of the Svāyambhuva Manu, there was a mighty Daitya,
Hiraṇyākṣa, of great splendor, endowed with the power of austerity.

5.121.s:
tairvyāptaṃ jagadetaddhi nirasya tridaśādhipam ..
yajña bhāgāścadevānāṃ hṛtā vīryaprabhāvataḥ .. 8 ..
5.121.d:
तैर्व्याप्तं जगदेतद्धि निरस्य त्रिदशाधिपम् ..
यज्ञ भागाश्चदेवानां हृता वीर्यप्रभावतः .. 8 ..
5.121.m:
Indeed, this world was pervaded by them after expelling the ruler of the gods,
and the sacrificial shares of the gods were seized by virtue of his valor.

5.121.s:
atha śakraḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ gaṃgādvāraṃ samāśritaḥ ..
tapastepe suduḥkhārto rājyaśrīparivarjitaḥ .. 9 ..
5.121.d:
अथ शक्रः सुरैः सार्धं गंगाद्वारं समाश्रितः ..
तपस्तेपे सुदुःखार्तो राज्यश्रीपरिवर्जितः .. 9 ..
5.121.m:
Then Śakra, along with the gods, took refuge at Gaṅgādvāra;
afflicted with great sorrow, deprived of the fortune of his kingdom, he performed austerity.

5.121.s:
tasyaivaṃ tapyamānasya tapastīvraṃ mahātmanaḥ ..
māhiṣaṃ rūpamāsthāya niścakrāma dharātalāt .. 6.122.10 ..
5.121.d:
तस्यैवं तप्यमानस्य तपस्तीव्रं महात्मनः ..
माहिषं रूपमास्थाय निश्चक्राम धरातलात् .. 6.122.10 ..
5.121.m:
As that noble-souled one was thus performing severe austerity,
assuming the form of a buffalo, he came forth from the surface of the earth.

5.121.s:
svayameva mahādevastataḥ śakramuvāca ha ..
kedārayāmi me śīghraṃ brūhi sarvaṃ surottama ..
daityānāmatha sarveṣāṃ rūpeṇānena vāsava .. 11 ..
5.121.d:
स्वयमेव महादेवस्ततः शक्रमुवाच ह ..
केदारयामि मे शीघ्रं ब्रूहि सर्वं सुरोत्तम ..
दैत्यानामथ सर्वेषां रूपेणानेन वासव .. 11 ..
5.121.m:
Mahādeva himself then spoke to Śakra:
“Whom do I tear apart? Tell me quickly, O best of gods,
among all the Daityas, O Vāsava, with this form?”

5.121.s:
.. indra uvāca .. ..
hiraṇyākṣo mahādaityaḥ subāhurvakra kandharaḥ ..
triśṛṃgo lohitākṣaśca paṃcaitāndāraya prabho ..
hatairetairhataṃ sarvaṃ dānavānāmasaṃśayam .. 12 ..
5.121.d:
.. इन्द्र उवाच .. ..
हिरण्याक्षो महादैत्यः सुबाहुर्वक्र कन्धरः ..
त्रिशृंगो लोहिताक्षश्च पंचैतान्दारय प्रभो ..
हतैरेतैर्हतं सर्वं दानवानामसंशयम् .. 12 ..
5.121.m:
Indra said:
“The great Daitya Hiraṇyākṣa, Subāhu, Vakragrīva,
Triśṛṅga, and Lohitākṣa—tear apart these five, O Lord.
When these are slain, all the Dānavas are slain beyond doubt.

5.121.s:
kimanyaiḥ kṛpaṇairdhvastairyaiḥ kiṃcinnātra sidhyati ..
tasya tadvacanaśrutvā bhagavāṃstūrṇamabhyagāt ..
yatra dānavamukhyo'sau hiraṇyākṣo mahābalaḥ .. 13 ..
5.121.d:
किमन्यैः कृपणैर्ध्वस्तैर्यैः किंचिन्नात्र सिध्यति ..
तस्य तद्वचनश्रुत्वा भगवांस्तूर्णमभ्यगात् ..
यत्र दानवमुख्योऽसौ हिरण्याक्षो महाबलः .. 13 ..
5.121.m:
What is the use of other wretched ones being destroyed, through whom nothing is accomplished here?”
Having heard that speech of his, the Blessed One went swiftly
to where that chief of Dānavas, the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa, was.

5.121.s:
atha taṃ dūrato dṛṣṭvā mahiṣaṃ parvatopamam ..
āyātaṃ raudrarūpeṇa dānavāḥ sarvataśca te .. 14 ..
5.121.d:
अथ तं दूरतो दृष्ट्वा महिषं पर्वतोपमम् ..
आयातं रौद्ररूपेण दानवाः सर्वतश्च ते .. 14 ..
5.121.m:
Then, seeing from afar that buffalo resembling a mountain
approaching in a terrible form, all those Dānavas on every side,

5.121.s:
tato jaghnuśca pāṣāṇairlaguḍaiśca tathāpare ..
kṣveḍitāsphoṭitāṃścakrustathānye balagarvitāḥ .. .. 15 ..
5.121.d:
ततो जघ्नुश्च पाषाणैर्लगुडैश्च तथापरे ..
क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितांश्चक्रुस्तथान्ये बलगर्विताः .. .. 15 ..
5.121.m:
struck [him] with stones, and others likewise with clubs;
and others, proud of their strength, gave war-whoops and clapped their arms.

5.121.s:
athavamanya tāndevaḥ prahāraṃ līlayā dadau ..
yatrāste dānavendro'sau caturbhiḥ sacivaiḥ saha .. 16 ...
5.121.d:
अथवमन्य तान्देवः प्रहारं लीलया ददौ ..
यत्रास्ते दानवेन्द्रोऽसौ चतुर्भिः सचिवैः सह .. 16 ...
5.121.m:
Then, disregarding them, the god effortlessly dealt a blow
where that lord of Dānavas sat with his four ministers.

5.121.s:
tataḥ śastraṃ samudyamya yāvaddhāvati sammukhaḥ ..
tāvacchṛṃgaprahāreṇa sonayadyamasādanam .. 17 ..
5.121.d:
ततः शस्त्रं समुद्यम्य यावद्धावति सम्मुखः ..
तावच्छृंगप्रहारेण सोनयद्यमसादनम् .. 17 ..
5.121.m:
Then, lifting his weapon, as he ran head-on,
he dispatched him to the abode of Yama with a thrust of his horn.

5.121.s:
hatvā taṃ sacivānpaścātsubāhupramukhāṃśca tān ..
jaghāna hanyamāno'pi samantāddānavaiḥ paraiḥ .. 18 ..
5.121.d:
हत्वा तं सचिवान्पश्चात्सुबाहुप्रमुखांश्च तान् ..
जघान हन्यमानोऽपि समन्ताद्दानवैः परैः .. 18 ..
5.121.m:
Having slain him, he afterwards struck down those ministers headed by Subāhu,
though he was being struck on all sides by the other Dānavas.

5.121.s:
na tasya lagate kvāpi śastraṃ gātre kathaṃcana ..
yatnato'pi visṛṣṭaṃ ca labdhalakṣaiḥ prahāribhiḥ .. 19 ..
5.121.d:
न तस्य लगते क्वापि शस्त्रं गात्रे कथंचन ..
यत्नतोऽपि विसृष्टं च लब्धलक्षैः प्रहारिभिः .. 19 ..
5.121.m:
No weapon whatsoever touched his body,
even when hurled with effort by skilled marksmen.

5.121.s:
evaṃ paṃca pradhānāstānhatvā daityānmaheśvaraḥ ..
bhūyo jagāma taṃ deśaṃ yatra śakro vyavasthitaḥ ..
abravīcca prahaṣṭātmā tataḥ śakraṃ taponvitam .. 6.122.20 ..
mayā te nihatāḥ paṃca dānavā ye tvayeritāḥ ..
tasmāttrailokyarājyaṃ svaṃ bhūya eva samācara ..2...
5.121.d:
एवं पंच प्रधानास्तान्हत्वा दैत्यान्महेश्वरः ..
भूयो जगाम तं देशं यत्र शक्रो व्यवस्थितः ..

went again to that place where Śakra was stationed,
and, with a delighted heart, he then spoke to Śakra, who was endowed with austerity:
“Those five Dānavas who were mentioned by you have been slain by me.
Therefore, conduct your rule over the three worlds once again.

hands, that man shall surely redeem his three families,
even if one of sinful conduct, even if dwelling in hell:
with the left, the maternal side; then with the right, the paternal;
and then himself with both hands, according to my word.”
Indra said:
“Coming daily from heaven, O you whose vehicle is the bull,
I shall worship you dwelling here, and I shall also drink the water.
Because it was spoken by you in the form of a buffalo, ‘Whom do I tear apart?’ (ke dārayāmi),
you shall therefore become renowned by the name Kedāra.”
The Blessed One said:
“If you do thus, O Śakra, then you will have no fear of the Daityas;
supreme splendor shall enter entirely into your body.”
Having been told this, the thousand-eyed one then constructed an excellent temple for him,
most pleasing to behold and enchanting.
Then, bowing to that god and taking leave of him thereafter,
he went to his own abode situated on the summit of Mount Meru.

5.121.m:
Then, coming daily from heaven, with concentrated mind,
he performed worship full of great devotion to the trident-bearing god Kedāra.
And having drunk the consecrated water three times, he departed, O best of brahmins.
Then after a certain time, as he arrived there,
that entire mountain peak was completely covered with snow,
and that pool, along with the temple and the god.
Then, overwhelmed with sorrow, filled with supreme devotion,
he bowed reverently toward that direction and went to his own abode.
As he thus kept coming, four months passed,
not seeing Mahādeva, his mind filled with longing to behold him.
Then, O brahmins, when summer arrived again in the Himālayas,
the god came into sight, stationed in that very form.
Then, having performed the great worship belonging to the four months,
he performed songs, instrumental music, and so on before him with faith.
