5.121.m:
Then, seeing the faith of that protector of cows, / the blessed destroyer of Tripura appeared before him and said:
"I am well pleased, O lord of gods, by this one-pointed devotion. / Therefore, ask for whatever desire is in your heart; I will grant it."
Śakra said: / "By your grace my unsurpassed sovereignty has come to be; / whatever exists in the three worlds, all that is established in my home.
Therefore, if you are pleased with me, O bull-bannered Lord, / or if, being gratified, you grant me a boon, then grant this wish of mine:
This mountain is accessible for eight months, O lord of gods, / as long as the sun, positioned in Pisces, moves forward—so I have heard.
After that, it becomes inaccessible, covered by an expanse of snow, / for four months, until the sun enters Aquarius.
It becomes inaccessible even to me, O destroyer of Tripura; / how much more so for men and others of feeble strength, O lord of gods!

5.121.m:
Therefore, in heaven, in Pātāla, or on earth, O lord of the thirty [gods], / remain in this form for four months, / so that my vow may not be broken, O lord of gods!"
Sūta said: / Then the god, having meditated for a long time, said to the slayer of Bala, / feeling supreme satisfaction, with a voice sounding like the roar of a cloud:
"In the Ānarta country, on the surface of the earth, / there is our sacred field named Hāṭakeśvara, O thousand-eyed one.
There I will always dwell, O Vāsava, when the sun is in Scorpio, / until the end of Aquarius, on account of your word, without a doubt.
Therefore, go there swiftly, erect a splendid temple, / install my form, and perform worship appropriately, / so that I may hold my own splendour there for your sake."
Sūta said: / Hearing this of the trident-bearing god of gods, / the thousand-eyed one went there and then carried out the word spoken by the god.

एवं स भगवांस्तत्र शक्रेणाराधितः पुरा ..
समायातोऽत्र विप्रेंद्राः सुरम्यात्तु हिमाचलात् .. 58 ..
यस्तमाराधयेत्सम्यक्सदा मासचतुष्टयम् ..
हिमपातोद्भवे मर्त्यः स शिवाय प्रपद्यते .. 59 ..
शेषकालेऽपि यः पूजां करोत्येव सुभक्तितः ..
स पापं क्षालयेत्प्राज्ञ आजन्ममरणांतिकम् .. 6.122.60 ..
तत्र गीतं प्रशंसंति नृत्यं चैव पृथग्विधम् ..
देवस्य पुरतः प्राज्ञाः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदाः .. 61 ..
अत्र श्लोकः पुरा गीतो नारदेन सुरर्षिणा ..
तद्वोऽहं कीर्तयिष्यामि श्रूयतां ब्राह्मणोत्तमाः .. 62 ..
5.121.m:
Having constructed the temple and installed the form of the trident-bearer, / he also made a pool of that form, filled with clear water.
Then he worshipped with flowers, incense, and unguents; / having bathed in the pool, he drank the water three times as before.
Thus the Blessed Lord was worshipped there by Śakra in ancient times, / having arrived there, O foremost of brahmins, from the lovely Himācala.
A mortal who properly worships him there constantly for four months / during the snowfall goes to Śiva.
Even at other times, whoever performs worship with deep devotion / washes away, O wise one, sin from birth until death.
Wise men skilled in all treatises / praise song and diverse kinds of dance there before the god.
On this matter, a verse was formerly sung by Nārada, the celestial seer; / that I will recite to you; let it be heard, O best of brahmins:

5.121.s:
kedāre salilaṃ pītvā gayāpiḍaṃ pradāya ca ..
brahmajñānamathāsādya punarjanma na vidyate .. 63 ..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ kedārasya ca saṃbhavam ..
ākhyānaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam .. 64 ..
yaścaitatchṛṇuyātsamyakpaṭhedvā tasya cāgrataḥ ..
śrāvayedvāpi vā viprāḥ sarvapātakanānam ..
kedārasya sa pāpaughairmucyate tatkṣaṇānnaraḥ .. 65 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṃḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye kedārotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmadvāviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 122 .. .. cha ..
5.121.d:
केदारे सलिलं पीत्वा गयापिडं प्रदाय च ..
ब्रह्मज्ञानमथासाद्य पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते .. 63 ..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं केदारस्य च संभवम् ..
आख्यानं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 64 ..
यश्चैतत्छृणुयात्सम्यक्पठेद्वा तस्य चाग्रतः ..
श्रावयेद्वापि वा विप्राः सर्वपातकनानम् ..
केदारस्य स पापौघैर्मुच्यते तत्क्षणान्नरः .. 65 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखंडे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये केदारोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामद्वाविंशत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 122 .. .. छ ..
5.121.m:
"Having drunk the water at Kedāra, and having offered a funerary ball at Gayā, / and having attained the knowledge of Brahman, there is no rebirth."
All this has been recounted to you regarding the origin of Kedāra, / a narrative that destroys all sins, O best of brahmins.
Whoever hears this properly, or reads it before him, / or causes it to be heard, O brahmins, [this story] of Kedāra that destroys all sins— / that man is instantly freed from the floods of sin.
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Origin and Māhātmya of Kedāra' in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.122.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathānyadapi tatrāsti śuklatīrthamanuttamam..
darbhaiḥ saṃsūcitaṃ śvetairyadadyāpi dvijottamāḥ .. 1 ..
5.122.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथान्यदपि तत्रास्ति शुक्लतीर्थमनुत्तमम्..
दर्भैः संसूचितं श्वेतैर्यदद्यापि द्विजोत्तमाः .. 1 ..
5.122.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, there is another unsurpassed sacred ford there, Śuklatīrtha, / indicated by white kuśa grass even today, O best of the twice-born.

5.122.s:
camatkārapure pūrvamāsītkaścitsuśalyavit ..
rajakaḥ śuddhakonāma putrapautrasamanvitaḥ .. .. 2..
5.122.d:
चमत्कारपुरे पूर्वमासीत्कश्चित्सुशल्यवित् ..
रजकः शुद्धकोनाम पुत्रपौत्रसमन्वितः .. .. 2..
5.122.m: Formerly, in Camatkārapura, there was an expert bone-setter, / a washerman named Śuddhaka, along with his sons and grandsons.

5.122.s:
sa sarvarajakānāṃ ca prādhānyena vyavasthitaḥ ..
pradhānabrāhmaṇānāṃ ca karotyaṃbaraśodhanam .. 3 ..
5.122.d:
स सर्वरजकानां च प्राधान्येन व्यवस्थितः ..
प्रधानब्राह्मणानां च करोत्यंबरशोधनम् .. 3 ..
5.122.m: He stood at the head of all the washermen, / and he cleansed the garments of the prominent brahmins.

5.122.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya nīlīkuṇḍyāṃ samāhitaḥ ..
prākṣipadbrāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ vāso vijñātavāṃścirāt .. 4 ..
5.122.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य नीलीकुण्ड्यां समाहितः ..
प्राक्षिपद्ब्राह्मणेंद्राणां वासो विज्ञातवांश्चिरात् .. 4 ..
5.122.m: Now, at a certain time, fixed in intent, into a vat of indigo / he cast the clothing of the foremost brahmins, [only] realising it after a long time.

5.122.s:
athāsau mandacittaśca svāmāhūyakuṭumbinīm ..
putrāṃśca vacanaṃ prāha rahasye bhayavihvalaḥ .. 5 ..
5.122.d:
अथासौ मन्दचित्तश्च स्वामाहूयकुटुम्बिनीम् ..
पुत्रांश्च वचनं प्राह रहस्ये भयविह्वलः .. 5 ..
5.122.m: Then, troubled in mind, he called his wife / and sons, and, overcome with fear, spoke these words in secret:

5.122.s:
nirmūlyāni suvastrāṇi brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām ..
nīlīmadhye vimohena prakṣiptāni bahūni ca .. 6 ..
5.122.d:
निर्मूल्यानि सुवस्त्राणि ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम् ..
नीलीमध्ये विमोहेन प्रक्षिप्तानि बहूनि च .. 6 ..
5.122.m: "Many priceless fine garments of the great-souled brahmins / have been thrown into the indigo by delusion.

5.122.s:
vadhabandhādikaṃ karma te kariṣyaṃtyasaṃśayam ..
tasmādanyatra gacchāmo gṛhītvā rajanīmimām .. 7 ..
5.122.d:
वधबन्धादिकं कर्म ते करिष्यंत्यसंशयम् ..
तस्मादन्यत्र गच्छामो गृहीत्वा रजनीमिमाम् .. 7 ..
5.122.m: They will undoubtedly carry out punishment such as killing and binding; / therefore, taking advantage of this night, let us go elsewhere."

5.122.s:
evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā sāramādāya maṃdirāt ..
prasthito bhāryayā sārddhaṃ kāṃdiśīko dvijottamāḥ .. 8 ..
5.122.d:
एवं स निश्चयं कृत्वा सारमादाय मंदिरात् ..
प्रस्थितो भार्यया सार्द्धं कांदिशीको द्विजोत्तमाः .. 8 ..
5.122.m: Having thus made a decision and taken the valuables from the house, / he set out with his wife, fleeing in terror, O best of the twice-born.

5.122.s:
tāvattasya sutā gatvā svāṃ sakhīṃ dāśasaṃbhavām ..
uvāca kṣamyatāṃ bhadre yanmayā kukṛtaṃ kṛtam.. 9 ..
5.122.d:
तावत्तस्य सुता गत्वा स्वां सखीं दाशसंभवाम् ..
उवाच क्षम्यतां भद्रे यन्मया कुकृतं कृतम्.. 9 ..
5.122.m: Meanwhile, his daughter went to her friend, a fisherman's daughter, / and said: "Forgive me, good friend, whatever wrong action I have done,

5.122.s:
ajñānājjñānato vāpi prakrīḍaṃtyā tvayā saha ..
praṇayādbālyabhāvācca krodhādvātha maherṣyayā .. 6.123.10 ..
5.122.d:
अज्ञानाज्ज्ञानतो वापि प्रक्रीडंत्या त्वया सह ..
प्रणयाद्बाल्यभावाच्च क्रोधाद्वाथ महेर्ष्यया .. 6.123.10 ..
5.122.m: whether unwittingly or wittingly while playing with you, / out of affection, childish nature, or through anger or great envy."

5.122.s:
atha sā sahasā śrutvā bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā ..
uvāca kimidaṃ bhadre yanmāmitthaṃ prabhāṣase .. 11 ..
5.122.d:
अथ सा सहसा श्रुत्वा बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा ..
उवाच किमिदं भद्रे यन्मामित्थं प्रभाषसे .. 11 ..
5.122.m: Then she, suddenly hearing this, with eyes bewildered by tears, / said: "What is this, good friend, that you speak to me in this manner?"

5.122.s:
.. sakhyuvāca .. ..
mama tātena nīlāyāṃ prakṣiptānyaṃbarāṇi ca ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ mahārhāṇi vibhrameṇa sulocane .. 12 ..
5.122.d:
.. सख्युवाच .. ..
मम तातेन नीलायां प्रक्षिप्तान्यंबराणि च ..
ब्राह्मणानां महार्हाणि विभ्रमेण सुलोचने .. 12 ..
5.122.m: The friend said: / "My father has thrown the costly garments of the brahmins / into indigo through an error, O fair-eyed one.

5.122.s:
tatprabhāte parijñāya daṃḍaṃ dhāsyaṃti dāruṇam ..
evaṃ citte samāsthāya tātaḥ saṃprasthito'dhunā .. 13 ..
5.122.d:
तत्प्रभाते परिज्ञाय दंडं धास्यंति दारुणम् ..
एवं चित्ते समास्थाय तातः संप्रस्थितोऽधुना .. 13 ..
5.122.m: Therefore, when they discover it in the morning, they will inflict severe punishment; / keeping this in mind, my father has now set out.

5.122.s:
ahaṃ tavātikaṃ prāptā darśanārthamanindite ..
anujñātā prayāsyāmi tvayā tasmātpramucyatām .. 14 ..
5.122.d:
अहं तवातिकं प्राप्ता दर्शनार्थमनिन्दिते ..
अनुज्ञाता प्रयास्यामि त्वया तस्मात्प्रमुच्यताम् .. 14 ..
5.122.m: I have come to your presence to see you, O blameless one; / having been permitted by you, I shall depart; therefore, let me go."

5.122.s:
atha sā tadvacaḥ śrutvā prasannavadanā'bravīt ..
yadyevaṃ mā sarojākṣi kutracitsaṃprayāsyasi .. 15 ..
5.122.d:
अथ सा तद्वचः श्रुत्वा प्रसन्नवदनाऽब्रवीत् ..
यद्येवं मा सरोजाक्षि कुत्रचित्संप्रयास्यसि .. 15 ..
5.122.m: Then she, hearing those words, said with a pleasant face: / "If that is so, do not go anywhere, O lotus-eyed one!

5.122.s:
nivāraya drutaṃ gatvā tātaṃ no gamyatāmiti ..
asti pūrvottare bhāge sthānādasmājjalāśayaḥ .. 16 ..
tatraikadā vinikṣiptaṃ mama tātena jālakam ..
atīvakṛṣṇakeśotthaṃ tāvacchuklatvamāgatam...7..
5.122.d:
निवारय द्रुतं गत्वा तातं नो गम्यतामिति ..
अस्ति पूर्वोत्तरे भागे स्थानादस्माज्जलाशयः .. 16 ..
तत्रैकदा विनिक्षिप्तं मम तातेन जालकम् ..
अतीवकृष्णकेशोत्थं तावच्छुक्लत्वमागतम्...7..
5.122.m:
Go quickly and stop your father, saying, 'We must not go.' / To the northeast of this place there is a reservoir of water.
Once, a net made of very black hair was cast in there / by my father, and at once it became white.

5.122.s:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sasnau kutūhalāt .
yāvacchuklatvamāpannastādṛkkṛṣṇavapurdharaḥ .. 19 ..
suśvetamūrdhajaḥ sadyaḥ strīṇāṃ vairāgyakārakaḥ ..
tataḥprabhṛti no jñātvā kaścittatra pragacchati .. 19 ..
5.122.d:
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टः स्वयं सस्नौ कुतूहलात् .
यावच्छुक्लत्वमापन्नस्तादृक्कृष्णवपुर्धरः .. 19 ..
सुश्वेतमूर्धजः सद्यः स्त्रीणां वैराग्यकारकः ..
ततःप्रभृति नो ज्ञात्वा कश्चित्तत्र प्रगच्छति .. 19 ..
5.122.m:
Then, filled with wonder, he bathed in it himself out of curiosity; / and while he had possessed such a dark body, he became white.
With hair turned bright white at once, an object of dispassion to women, / from that time forward no one, upon learning this, goes there.

5.122.s:
tasmāttatraiva vastrāṇi prakṣālayatu satvaram ..
tātaḥ sa tava yāsyaṃti viśuddhiṃ paramāṃ śubhe .. 6.123.20 ..
5.122.d:
तस्मात्तत्रैव वस्त्राणि प्रक्षालयतु सत्वरम् ..
तातः स तव यास्यंति विशुद्धिं परमां शुभे .. 6.123.20 ..
5.122.m: Therefore, O fair one, let that father of yours wash the clothes / there without delay; they will attain the highest purity.”

5.122.s:
atha sā satvaraṃ gatvā nijatātasya tadvacaḥ ..
satvaraṃ kathayāmāsa prahṛṣṭavadanā satī .. 21
5.122.d:
अथ सा सत्वरं गत्वा निजतातस्य तद्वचः ..
सत्वरं कथयामास प्रहृष्टवदना सती .. 21
5.122.m: Then she quickly went and reported that advice / to her own father in haste, her face beaming with joy, the virtuous girl [saying]:

5.122.s:
mama sakhyā samādiṣṭaṃ nātidūre jalāśayaḥ ..
tatra śvetatvamāyāti sarvaṃ kṣiptaṃ sitetaram ..22..
5.122.d:
मम सख्या समादिष्टं नातिदूरे जलाशयः ..
तत्र श्वेतत्वमायाति सर्वं क्षिप्तं सितेतरम् ..22..
5.122.m: “My friend has directed that not far away is a pool of water; / whatever is other than white, when cast in there, becomes white.

5.122.s:
tasmātprakṣālaya prātastatra gatvā jalāśaye ..
vastrāṇyamūni śuklatvaṃ saṃprayāsyaṃtyasaṃśayam.. 23..
5.122.d:
तस्मात्प्रक्षालय प्रातस्तत्र गत्वा जलाशये ..
वस्त्राण्यमूनि शुक्लत्वं संप्रयास्यंत्यसंशयम्.. 23..
5.122.m: Therefore, go to that pool in the morning and wash / these clothes; they will undoubtedly become white.”

5.122.s:
.. rajaka uvāca ..
naitatsaṃpatsyate putri yannīlasya parikṣayaḥ ..
vastralagnasya jāyeta yataḥ proktaṃ purātanaiḥ ..24..
5.122.d:
.. रजक उवाच ..
नैतत्संपत्स्यते पुत्रि यन्नीलस्य परिक्षयः ..
वस्त्रलग्नस्य जायेत यतः प्रोक्तं पुरातनैः ..24..
5.122.m: The washerman said: / “This will not happen, daughter, that indigo / clinging to a garment would be eradicated; for it has been said by the ancients:

5.122.s:
vajralepasya mūrkhasya nārīṇāṃ karkaṭasya ca ..
eko grahastu mīnānāṃ nīlīmadyapayostathā ..25..
5.122.d:
वज्रलेपस्य मूर्खस्य नारीणां कर्कटस्य च ..
एको ग्रहस्तु मीनानां नीलीमद्यपयोस्तथा ..25..
5.122.m: ‘The grasp of diamond-cement, of a fool, of women, and of a crab / is single, as is that of fish, and likewise of indigo and wine.’ ”

5.122.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
tatra hyāgamyatāṃ tāvadvastraṇayādāya yatnataḥ ..
toyācchuddhiṃ prayāsyaṃti tadā''gaṃtavyameva hi .. ..26..
5.122.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
तत्र ह्यागम्यतां तावद्वस्त्रणयादाय यत्नतः ..
तोयाच्छुद्धिं प्रयास्यंति तदा'ऽगंतव्यमेव हि .. ..26..
5.122.m: The maiden said: / “Come there then, having taken the clothes with care! / If they attain purity from the water, only then should we return home,

5.122.s:
bhūyo'pi maṃdire vā'tha tasmātsthānāddigaṃtaram ..
gaṃtavyaṃ sakalaireva mamaitaddhṛdi saṃsthitam..27..
5.122.d:
भूयोऽपि मंदिरे वाऽथ तस्मात्स्थानाद्दिगंतरम् ..
गंतव्यं सकलैरेव ममैतद्धृदि संस्थितम्..27..
5.122.m: or else from that place we must all go to another region; / this is what is fixed in my heart.”

5.122.s:
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā sādhusādhviti te'sakṛt ..
procya bāṃdhavabhṛtyāśca rātrāveva prajagmire ..28..
5.122.d:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा साधुसाध्विति तेऽसकृत् ..
प्रोच्य बांधवभृत्याश्च रात्रावेव प्रजग्मिरे ..28..
5.122.m: Hearing her words, saying repeatedly, “Good! Good!”, / the kinsmen and servants departed that very night,

5.122.s:
dāśakanyāṃ puraḥ kṛtvā saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ ..
vibhavena samāyuktā nijena dvijasattamāḥ ..29..
5.122.d:
दाशकन्यां पुरः कृत्वा संशयं परमं गताः ..
विभवेन समायुक्ता निजेन द्विजसत्तमाः ..29..
5.122.m: keeping the fisherman’s daughter in front, filled with utmost doubt, / accompanied by their possessions, O best of brahmins.

5.122.s:
tataḥ sā darśayāmāsa dāśakanyā jalāśayam ..
bahuvīrudhasaṃchannaṃ duṣpraveśaṃ ca dehinām .. 6.123.30 ..
5.122.d:
ततः सा दर्शयामास दाशकन्या जलाशयम् ..
बहुवीरुधसंछन्नं दुष्प्रवेशं च देहिनाम् .. 6.123.30 ..
5.122.m: Then the fisherman’s daughter showed them the pool of water, / overgrown with many creepers and difficult for embodied beings to enter.

5.122.s:
tataḥ sa rajakastatra vastrāṇyādāya sarvaśaḥ ..
praviṣṭaḥ salile tasminkṣālayāmāsa vai dvijāḥ .. 31 ..
5.122.d:
ततः स रजकस्तत्र वस्त्राण्यादाय सर्वशः ..
प्रविष्टः सलिले तस्मिन्क्षालयामास वै द्विजाः .. 31 ..
5.122.m: Then the washerman, taking all the clothes, / entered that water, O brahmins, and washed them.

5.122.s:
atha tāni suvastrāṇi mecakābhāni tatkṣaṇāt ..
jātāni sphaṭikābhāni tatkṣaṇādeva kṛtsnaśaḥ .. .. 32 ..
5.122.d:
अथ तानि सुवस्त्राणि मेचकाभानि तत्क्षणात् ..
जातानि स्फटिकाभानि तत्क्षणादेव कृत्स्नशः .. .. 32 ..
5.122.m: Then those fine garments, dark-hued as they were, instantly / became bright as crystal at that very moment, entirely so.

5.122.s:
tatastuṣṭisamāyuktaḥ sādhusādhviti cā'bravīt ..
samāliṃgya sutāṃ prāha dāśakanyāṃ ca sādaram .. 33 ..
5.122.d:
ततस्तुष्टिसमायुक्तः साधुसाध्विति चाऽब्रवीत् ..
समालिंग्य सुतां प्राह दाशकन्यां च सादरम् .. 33 ..
5.122.m: Then, filled with satisfaction, saying “Well done! Well done!”, / he embraced his daughter and respectfully addressed the fisherman’s daughter:

5.122.s: suvastrāṇi dvijeṃdrāṇāmarpayāmo yathākramam .. 34 ..
5.122.d: सुवस्त्राणि द्विजेंद्राणामर्पयामो यथाक्रमम् .. 34 ..
5.122.m: “Let us deliver the fine clothes to the lords of brahmins in proper order.”

5.122.s:
tataḥ sa svagṛhaṃ gatvā tāni vastrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
yathākrameṇa saṃhṛṣṭaḥ pradadau dvijasattamāḥ .. 35 ..
5.122.d:
ततः स स्वगृहं गत्वा तानि वस्त्राणि कृत्स्नशः ..
यथाक्रमेण संहृष्टः प्रददौ द्विजसत्तमाः .. 35 ..
5.122.m: Then, going to his own house, he, rejoiced, / gave back all those clothes in proper order, O best of brahmins.

5.122.s:
atha te brāhmaṇā dṛṣṭvā tāṃ śuddhiṃ vastrasaṃbhavām ..
taṃ ca śvetīkṛtaṃ cedṛgrajakaṃ vismayānvitāḥ .. 36 ..
5.122.d:
अथ ते ब्राह्मणा दृष्ट्वा तां शुद्धिं वस्त्रसंभवाम् ..
तं च श्वेतीकृतं चेदृग्रजकं विस्मयान्विताः .. 36 ..
5.122.m: Then those brahmins, seeing that cleanliness of the garments / and such a washerman turned white, were filled with astonishment.

5.122.s:
papracchuḥ kimidaṃ citraṃ vastramūrdhajasaṃbhavam ..
anaupamyaṃ ca saṃjātaṃ vadasva yadi manyase .. 37 ..
5.122.d:
पप्रच्छुः किमिदं चित्रं वस्त्रमूर्धजसंभवम् ..
अनौपम्यं च संजातं वदस्व यदि मन्यसे .. 37 ..
5.122.m: They asked: “What is this wondrous thing concerning the clothes and [your] hair? / An incomparable thing has occurred; tell us, if you please.”

5.122.s:
.. rajaka uvāca .. ..
etāni viprā vastrāṇi mayā kṣiptāni mohataḥ ..
nīlīmadhye suvastrāṇi vinaṣṭāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ .. .. 38 ..
5.122.d:
.. रजक उवाच .. ..
एतानि विप्रा वस्त्राणि मया क्षिप्तानि मोहतः ..
नीलीमध्ये सुवस्त्राणि विनष्टानि च कृत्स्नशः .. .. 38 ..
5.122.m: The washerman said: / “O brahmins, through delusion these fine garments were thrown by me / into the indigo, and were completely ruined.

5.122.s:
tato bhayaṃ mahadbhūtaṃ kuṭumbena samanvitaḥ ..
calito rajanīvaktre digaṃte brāhmaṇottamāḥ .. 39 ..
5.122.d:
ततो भयं महद्भूतं कुटुम्बेन समन्वितः ..
चलितो रजनीवक्त्रे दिगंते ब्राह्मणोत्तमाः .. 39 ..
5.122.m: Then great fear arose, and together with my family / I set out at nightfall for a distant quarter, O best of brahmins.

5.122.s:
athaiṣā tanayā'smākaṃ gatā nijasakhīṃ prati ..
dāśātmajāṃ suduḥkhārtā punardarśanalālasā .. 6.123.40 ..
5.122.d:
अथैषा तनयाऽस्माकं गता निजसखीं प्रति ..
दाशात्मजां सुदुःखार्ता पुनर्दर्शनलालसा .. 6.123.40 ..
5.122.m: Then this daughter of ours, deeply stricken with grief, / went to her friend, the fisherman's daughter, eager to see her again.

5.122.s:
tayā sarvamabhiprāyaṃ jñātvā me duḥkhahetukam ..
tataḥ saṃdarśayāmāsa sthitāgre svajalāśayam .. 41 ..
5.122.d:
तया सर्वमभिप्रायं ज्ञात्वा मे दुःखहेतुकम् ..
ततः संदर्शयामास स्थिताग्रे स्वजलाशयम् .. 41 ..
5.122.m: Having learned from her all the intention and the cause of my grief, / she, standing before her, then showed her own pool of water.

5.122.s:
tasminprakṣiptamātrāṇi vastrāṇīmāni tatkṣaṇāt ..
īdṛgvarṇāni jātāni vismayasya hi kāraṇam .. 42 ..
5.122.d:
तस्मिन्प्रक्षिप्तमात्राणि वस्त्राणीमानि तत्क्षणात् ..
ईदृग्वर्णानि जातानि विस्मयस्य हि कारणम् .. 42 ..
5.122.m: The moment these garments were thrown into it, / they instantly took on such a colour, truly a cause for wonder!

5.122.s:
tathā me mūrdhajāḥ kṛṣṇāstatra snātasya tatkṣaṇāt ..
paraṃ śuklatvamāpannā etatproktaṃ mayā sphuṭam .. 43 ..
5.122.d:
तथा मे मूर्धजाः कृष्णास्तत्र स्नातस्य तत्क्षणात् ..
परं शुक्लत्वमापन्ना एतत्प्रोक्तं मया स्फुटम् .. 43 ..
5.122.m: Likewise, my dark hair, as I bathed there, instantly / attained supreme whiteness; this has been clearly told by me.”

5.122.s:
evaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ śrutvā kautūhalasamanvitāḥ ..
tatra jagmuḥ parīkṣārthaṃ vikṣipya tadanaṃtaram .. 44 ..
5.122.d:
एवं ते ब्राह्मणाः श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्विताः ..
तत्र जग्मुः परीक्षार्थं विक्षिप्य तदनंतरम् .. 44 ..
5.122.m: Hearing this, those brahmins, filled with curiosity, / went there to test it, and cast in subsequently

5.122.s:
kṛṣṇadravyāṇi bhūrīṇi keśādīni sahasraśaḥ ..
sarvaṃ tacchuklatāṃ yāti tyaktvā varṇaṃ malīmasam .. 45 ..
5.122.d:
कृष्णद्रव्याणि भूरीणि केशादीनि सहस्रशः ..
सर्वं तच्छुक्लतां याति त्यक्त्वा वर्णं मलीमसम् .. 45 ..
5.122.m: many dark substances, hair and the like, by the thousands; / all of that turned white, shedding its dirty hue.

5.122.s:
tato vṛddhatayā ye ca viśeṣācchvetamūrdhajāḥ ..
te sasnuḥ śraddhayā yuktāstaruṇāścāpi dharmiṇaḥ .. 46 ..
5.122.d:
ततो वृद्धतया ये च विशेषाच्छ्वेतमूर्धजाः ..
ते सस्नुः श्रद्धया युक्तास्तरुणाश्चापि धर्मिणः .. 46 ..
5.122.m: Then those who had white hair especially on account of old age, / and righteous youths as well, bathed there with faith.

5.122.s:
tataḥ śuklatvamāpannāstejovīryasamanvitāḥ ..
bhavaṃti tatprabhāvena prayāṃti ca parāṃ gatim . 47 ..
5.122.d:
ततः शुक्लत्वमापन्नास्तेजोवीर्यसमन्विताः ..
भवंति तत्प्रभावेन प्रयांति च परां गतिम् . 47 ..
5.122.m: Then, having attained whiteness, endowed with fiery energy and vigour / by its power, they reach the highest state.

5.122.s:
atha tadvāsavo dṛṣṭvā śuklatīrthaṃ pramuktidam ..
pūrayāmāsa rajasā mānuṣotthabhayena ca .. 48 ..
5.122.d:
अथ तद्वासवो दृष्ट्वा शुक्लतीर्थं प्रमुक्तिदम् ..
पूरयामास रजसा मानुषोत्थभयेन च .. 48 ..
5.122.m: Then Indra, seeing that Śuklatīrtha which bestows ultimate liberation, / filled it with dust out of fear arising from mortals.

5.122.s:
adyāpi tatra yatkiṃcijjāyate'tha tṛṇādikam ..
tatsarvaṃ śuklatāmeti tattoyasya prabhāvataḥ .. 49 ..
tatrotthairyaḥ kuśaiḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute śraddhayānvitaḥ .3
5.122.d:
अद्यापि तत्र यत्किंचिज्जायतेऽथ तृणादिकम् ..
तत्सर्वं शुक्लतामेति तत्तोयस्य प्रभावतः .. 49 ..
तत्रोत्थैर्यः कुशैः श्राद्धं कुरुते श्रद्धयान्वितः .3
5.122.m:
Even today, whatever grass and the like grows there, / all of it turns white due to the power of that water.
Whoever performs a śrāddha with devotion using the kuśa grass grown there,

5.122.s: śvaitaistaistārayetsarvānpitṝnnarakagānapi . 6.123.50 ..
5.122.d: श्वैतैस्तैस्तारयेत्सर्वान्पितॄन्नरकगानपि . 6.123.50 ..
5.122.m: by means of those white blades would deliver all his ancestors, even those who have gone to hell.

5.122.s:
tattīrthotthāṃ mṛdaṃ gātre yojayitvā narottamaḥ ..
snānaṃ karoti tīrthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ labhate phalam .. 51 ..
5.122.d:
तत्तीर्थोत्थां मृदं गात्रे योजयित्वा नरोत्तमः ..
स्नानं करोति तीर्थानां सर्वेषां लभते फलम् .. 51 ..
5.122.m: The best of men who, applying to his body the mud originating from that sacred ford, / takes a bath, obtains the fruit of all sacred fords.

5.122.s:
yastairdarbhairnaro bhaktyā tilaiścāraṇyasaṃbhavaiḥ ..
karoti tarpaṇaṃ viprāḥ sa prīṇāti pitāmahān .. 52 ..
5.122.d:
यस्तैर्दर्भैर्नरो भक्त्या तिलैश्चारण्यसंभवैः ..
करोति तर्पणं विप्राः स प्रीणाति पितामहान् .. 52 ..
5.122.m: The man who with devotion offers a tarpaṇa with that darbha grass / and with wild-grown sesamum seeds, O brahmins, gladdens the ancestors.

5.122.s:
athāśvamedhātsaṃprāpyaṃ gayāśrāddhena yatphalam ..
nīlasaṃjñagavotsarge tathātrāpi dvijottamāḥ .. 53 ..
5.122.d:
अथाश्वमेधात्संप्राप्यं गयाश्राद्धेन यत्फलम् ..
नीलसंज्ञगवोत्सर्गे तथात्रापि द्विजोत्तमाः .. 53 ..
5.122.m: Moreover, whatever fruit is obtained from a horse-sacrifice, from a śrāddha at Gayā, / and likewise from releasing a dark-coloured bull, is obtained here, O best of brahmins.

5.122.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. .
śuklatīrthaṃ kathaṃ jātaṃ tatra tvaṃ sūtanaṃdana ..
vistareṇa samācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ .. 54 ..
5.122.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. .
शुक्लतीर्थं कथं जातं तत्र त्वं सूतनंदन ..
विस्तरेण समाचक्ष्व परं कौतूहलं हि नः .. 54 ..
5.122.m: The seers said: / “How did the Śuklatīrtha come to be there? O delight of Sūta, / describe it in detail, for our curiosity is immense.”

5.122.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
śvetadvīpaḥ samānīto viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
tatkṣetre kalibhītena yathā śauklyaṃ na saṃtyajet .. 55 ..
5.122.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
श्वेतद्वीपः समानीतो विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ..
तत्क्षेत्रे कलिभीतेन यथा शौक्ल्यं न संत्यजेत् .. 55 ..
5.122.m: Sūta said: / “Śvetadvīpa was brought by the almighty Viṣṇu / to that sacred field, out of fear of the Kali age, so that it might not lose its whiteness.

5.122.s:
kalikālena saṃspṛṣṭaḥ śvetadvīpo'pi śyāmatām ..
na prayāti dvijaśreṣṭhāstatastatra niveśitaḥ .. 56 ..
5.122.d:
कलिकालेन संस्पृष्टः श्वेतद्वीपोऽपि श्यामताम् ..
न प्रयाति द्विजश्रेष्ठास्ततस्तत्र निवेशितः .. 56 ..
5.122.m: Even when touched by the Kali age, Śvetadvīpa does not turn / black, O best of brahmins; therefore it was placed there.”

5.122.s: itiśrīskāṃdemahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śuklatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma trayoviṃśatyuttara śatatamodhyāyaḥ .. 123 .. .. cha ..
5.122.d: इतिश्रीस्कांदेमहापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शुक्लतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रयोविंशत्युत्तर शततमोध्यायः .. 123 .. .. छ ..
5.122.m: Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of Śuklatīrtha', in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.123.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
athānyadapi tatrāsti mukhāraṃ tīrthamuttamam ..
yatra te munayaḥ śreṣṭhā viprāścaureṇa saṃgatāḥ.....
yatra siddhiṃ samāpannaḥ sa caurastatprabhāvataḥ.
vālmīkiriti vikhyāto rāmāyaṇanibaṃdhakṛt..2..
5.123.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथान्यदपि तत्रास्ति मुखारं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
यत्र ते मुनयः श्रेष्ठा विप्राश्चौरेण संगताः.....
यत्र सिद्धिं समापन्नः स चौरस्तत्प्रभावतः.
वाल्मीकिरिति विख्यातो रामायणनिबंधकृत्..2..
5.123.m: Sūta said: / “Now there is another excellent sacred ford there, Mukhāra, / where those excellent sages and brahmins met with a thief, / [and] where, by its power, that thief attained perfection / and became famous as Vālmīki, the composer of the Rāmāyaṇa.”

5.123.s:
camatkārapure pūrvaṃ māṃḍavyānvaya saṃbhavaḥ ..
lohajaṃgho dvijo hyāsītpitṛmātṛparāyaṇaḥ ..3..
5.123.d:
चमत्कारपुरे पूर्वं मांडव्यान्वय संभवः ..
लोहजंघो द्विजो ह्यासीत्पितृमातृपरायणः ..3..
5.123.m: Formerly in Camatkārapura there was a twice-born named Lohajaṅgha, / born in the lineage of Māṇḍavya, who was devoted to his father and mother.

5.123.s:
tasyaikā cābhavatpatnī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī..
pativratā patiprāṇā patipriyahite ratā ..4..
5.123.d:
तस्यैका चाभवत्पत्नी प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी..
पतिव्रता पतिप्राणा पतिप्रियहिते रता ..4..
5.123.m: And he had a wife dearer to him even than life, / devoted to her husband, having her husband as her life, intent upon what was pleasing and beneficial to her husband.

5.123.s:
atha tasya sthitasyātra brahmavṛttyābhivartataḥ ..
jagāma sumahānkālaḥ pitṛmātṛratasya ca ..5..
5.123.d:
अथ तस्य स्थितस्यात्र ब्रह्मवृत्त्याभिवर्ततः ..
जगाम सुमहान्कालः पितृमातृरतस्य च ..5..
5.123.m: Now, as he dwelt there living by the livelihood of a brahmin, / devoted to his father and mother, a great deal of time passed.

5.123.s:
ekadā bhagavāñchakro na vavarṣa dharātale ..
ānartaviṣaye kṛtsne yāvadvādaśavatsarāḥ .. 6 ..
5.123.d:
एकदा भगवाञ्छक्रो न ववर्ष धरातले ..
आनर्तविषये कृत्स्ने यावद्वादशवत्सराः .. 6 ..
5.123.m: Once the lord Śakra did not rain upon the surface of the earth, / throughout the whole region of Ānarta, for as long as twelve years.

5.123.s:
tataḥ sa kaṣṭamāpanno lohajaṃgho dvijottamāḥ ..
na prāpnoti kvacidbhikṣāṃ na ca kiṃcitpratigraham .. 7 ..
5.123.d:
ततः स कष्टमापन्नो लोहजंघो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
न प्राप्नोति क्वचिद्भिक्षां न च किंचित्प्रतिग्रहम् .. 7 ..
5.123.m: Then Lohajaṅgha fell into distress, O best of brahmins; / he obtained no alms anywhere, nor any gift.

5.123.s:
tatastau pitarau dvau tu dṛṣṭvā kṣutparipīḍitau ..
bhāryāṃ ca ciṃtayāmāsa duḥkhena mahatānvitaḥ .. 8 ..
5.123.d:
ततस्तौ पितरौ द्वौ तु दृष्ट्वा क्षुत्परिपीडितौ ..
भार्यां च चिंतयामास दुःखेन महतान्वितः .. 8 ..
5.123.m: Then, seeing both his parents tormented by hunger / and his wife as well, filled with great sorrow, he thought:

5.123.s:
kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ syāddarśanaṃ mama ..
etābhyāmapi vṛddhābhyāṃ patnyāścaiva viśeṣataḥ .. 9 ..
5.123.d:
किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि कथं स्याद्दर्शनं मम ..
एताभ्यामपि वृद्धाभ्यां पत्न्याश्चैव विशेषतः .. 9 ..
5.123.m: “What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can I show my face / to both these elderly people, and especially to my wife?”

5.123.s:
tataḥ sa duḥkhasaṃyuktaḥ phalārthaṃ prayayau vane ..
na ca kiṃcidavāpnoti sarve śuṣkā mahīruhāḥ .. 6.124.10 ..
5.123.d:
ततः स दुःखसंयुक्तः फलार्थं प्रययौ वने ..
न च किंचिदवाप्नोति सर्वे शुष्का महीरुहाः .. 6.124.10 ..
5.123.m: Then, stricken with grief, he went into the forest for fruit, / but found nothing at all; all the trees were withered.

5.123.s:
athāpaśyatsa vṛddhāṃ strīṃ stokasasyasamanvitām ..
gacchamānāṃ tathā tena śrameṇa mahatānvitām ......
tatastatsasyamādāya vastrāṇi ca sa nirdayaḥ..
jagāma svagṛhaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ pitṛbhyāṃ ca nyavedayat..12..
5.123.d:
अथापश्यत्स वृद्धां स्त्रीं स्तोकसस्यसमन्विताम् ..
गच्छमानां तथा तेन श्रमेण महतान्विताम् ......
ततस्तत्सस्यमादाय वस्त्राणि च स निर्दयः..
जगाम स्वगृहं हृष्टः पितृभ्यां च न्यवेदयत्..12..
5.123.m: Then he saw an old woman carrying a small amount of grain, / walking along, overcome with great fatigue. / Thereupon, taking that grain and her clothes, that pitiless man / went home delighted and offered it to his parents.

5.123.s:
sa evaṃ labdhalakṣo'pi dasyukarmaṇi nityaśaḥ.
kṛtvā cauryaṃ pupoṣātha nijameva kuṭumbakam..13.
5.123.d:
स एवं लब्धलक्षोऽपि दस्युकर्मणि नित्यशः.
कृत्वा चौर्यं पुपोषाथ निजमेव कुटुम्बकम्..13.
5.123.m: Having thus found an opportunity, constantly engaged in the work of a bandit, / committing robbery, he maintained his own family.

5.123.s:
subhikṣe cāpi saṃprāpte nānyatkarma karoti saḥ.
brāhmīṃ vṛttiṃ parityaktvā cauryakarma samācarat..14..
5.123.d:
सुभिक्षे चापि संप्राप्ते नान्यत्कर्म करोति सः.
ब्राह्मीं वृत्तिं परित्यक्त्वा चौर्यकर्म समाचरत्..14..
5.123.m: And even when plenty returned, he did no other work; / abandoning the way of life of a brahmin, he practiced the deed of robbery.

5.123.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya tīrthayātrāprasaṃgataḥ.
tatra saptarṣayaḥ prāptā marīcipramukhā dvijāḥ..15..
5.123.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगतः.
तत्र सप्तर्षयः प्राप्ता मरीचिप्रमुखा द्विजाः..15..
5.123.m: Then, after some time, by way of pilgrimage to sacred fords, / the seven seers, brahmins headed by Marīci, arrived there.

5.123.s:
tatastānvijane dṛṣṭvā drohakopasamanvitaḥ.
yaṣṭimudyamya vegena tiṣṭhadhvamiti cābravīt..16..
5.123.d:
ततस्तान्विजने दृष्ट्वा द्रोहकोपसमन्वितः.
यष्टिमुद्यम्य वेगेन तिष्ठध्वमिति चाब्रवीत्..16..
5.123.m: Then, seeing them in an isolated place, filled with malice and rage, / raising his staff with haste, he said, “Halt!”

5.123.s:
triśikhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā satvaraṃ samupādravat.
bhartsamānaḥ sa paruṣairvākyaistāṃstāḍayanniva..17..
5.123.d:
त्रिशिखां भृकुटीं कृत्वा सत्वरं समुपाद्रवत्.
भर्त्समानः स परुषैर्वाक्यैस्तांस्ताडयन्निव..17..
5.123.m: Knitting his brows into three points, he rushed forward swiftly, / threatening them with harsh words, as if striking them.

5.123.s:
tataste munayo dṛṣṭvā yamadūtopamaṃ ca tam.
yajñopavītasaṃyuktaṃ procuste kṛpayānvitāḥ..18..
5.123.d:
ततस्ते मुनयो दृष्ट्वा यमदूतोपमं च तम्.
यज्ञोपवीतसंयुक्तं प्रोचुस्ते कृपयान्विताः..18..
5.123.m: Then those sages, seeing him resembling a messenger of Yama / yet endowed with the sacred thread, spoke, filled with compassion.

5.123.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
aho tvaṃ brāhmaṇo'sīti tatkasmādatigarhitam.
karoṣi karma caitaddhi mlecchakṛtyaṃ tu bāliśa..19..
5.123.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः..
अहो त्वं ब्राह्मणोऽसीति तत्कस्मादतिगर्हितम्.
करोषि कर्म चैतद्धि म्लेच्छकृत्यं तु बालिश..19..
5.123.m: The seers said: / “Ah, you are a brahmin! Why then do you perform this utterly despicable / deed, which is an action of barbarians, O foolish one?

5.123.s:
vayaṃ ca munayaḥ śāṃtāstyaktā'śeṣaparigrahāḥ.
nāsmākamapi pārśvasthaṃ kiṃcidgṛhṇāti yadbhavanān.6.124.20..
5.123.d:
वयं च मुनयः शांतास्त्यक्ताऽशेषपरिग्रहाः.
नास्माकमपि पार्श्वस्थं किंचिद्गृह्णाति यद्भवनान्.6.124.20..
5.123.m: And we are peaceful sages who have renounced all possessions; / there is nothing by our side for you to take.”

5.123.s:
lohajaṃgha uvāca.
etāni śubhracīrāṇi valkalānyajināni ca.
upānahasametāni śīghraṃ yacchaṃtu me dvijāḥ..21...
5.123.d:
लोहजंघ उवाच.
एतानि शुभ्रचीराणि वल्कलान्यजिनानि च.
उपानहसमेतानि शीघ्रं यच्छंतु मे द्विजाः..21...
5.123.m: Lohajaṅgha said: / “Give me quickly, O brahmins, these clean rags, / bark garments, and deerskins, together with sandals!

5.123.s:
no ceddhatvāprahāreṇa yaṣṭyā vajropamena ca ..
prāpayiṣyasyasaṃdigdhaṃ dharmarājaniveśanam .. 22 ..
5.123.d:
नो चेद्धत्वाप्रहारेण यष्ट्या वज्रोपमेन च ..
प्रापयिष्यस्यसंदिग्धं धर्मराजनिवेशनम् .. 22 ..
5.123.m: If not, having struck you down with a blow of my staff like a thunderbolt, / I will send you, without doubt, to the abode of the King of Justice!”

5.123.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
sarvaṃ dāsyāmahe tubhyaṃ vayaṃ tāvanmalimluca ..
kiṃvadantīṃ vadāsmākaṃ yāṃ pṛcchāmaḥ kutūhalāt .. 23 ..
5.123.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः ..
सर्वं दास्यामहे तुभ्यं वयं तावन्मलिम्लुच ..
किंवदन्तीं वदास्माकं यां पृच्छामः कुतूहलात् .. 23 ..
5.123.m: The seers said: / “We will give everything to you, O robber; / first tell us the report about which we ask out of curiosity:

5.123.s:
kimarthaṃ kuruṣe cauryaṃ tvaṃ vipro'si sunirghṛṇaḥ ..
kiṃ jito vyasanai raudraiḥ kiṃ vā vyādhadvijo bhavān ..24..
5.123.d:
किमर्थं कुरुषे चौर्यं त्वं विप्रोऽसि सुनिर्घृणः ..
किं जितो व्यसनै रौद्रैः किं वा व्याधद्विजो भवान् ..24..
5.123.m: For what purpose do you commit robbery, being a brahmin utterly without pity? / Have you been overcome by terrible vices, or are you a hunter-brahmin?”

5.123.s:
.. lohajaṃgha uvāca .. ..
vyasanārthaṃ na me kṛtyametaccauryasamudbhavam ..
kuṭumbārthaṃ vijānītha dharmametanna saṃśayaḥ .. 25 ..
5.123.d:
.. लोहजंघ उवाच .. ..
व्यसनार्थं न मे कृत्यमेतच्चौर्यसमुद्भवम् ..
कुटुम्बार्थं विजानीथ धर्ममेतन्न संशयः .. 25 ..
5.123.m: Lohajaṅgha said: / “This undertaking born of theft is not for the sake of vice; / know that it is for the sake of my family; this is duty, no doubt.

5.123.s:
pitarau mama vārddhakye vartamānau vyavasthitau ..
tathā pativratā patnī gṛhadharmavicakṣaṇā .. 26 ..
5.123.d:
पितरौ मम वार्द्धक्ये वर्तमानौ व्यवस्थितौ ..
तथा पतिव्रता पत्नी गृहधर्मविचक्षणा .. 26 ..
5.123.m: My parents are both dwelling in old age, / and likewise my devoted wife is discerning in the duties of the household.

5.123.s:
upārjjayāmi yatkiñcidahametena karmaṇā ..
tatsarvaṃ tatkṛte nūnaṃ satyenātmānamālabhe ..27..
5.123.d:
उपार्ज्जयामि यत्किञ्चिदहमेतेन कर्मणा ..
तत्सर्वं तत्कृते नूनं सत्येनात्मानमालभे ..27..
5.123.m: Whatever I earn through this action, / all that is certainly for their sake; I swear upon my own soul!

5.123.s:
tasmānmuṃcatha prāksarvaṃ vibhavaṃ kiṃ vṛthoktibhiḥ ..
kṛtābhiḥ sphurate hasto mamāyaṃ hantumeva hi ..28.. ..
5.123.d:
तस्मान्मुंचथ प्राक्सर्वं विभवं किं वृथोक्तिभिः ..
कृताभिः स्फुरते हस्तो ममायं हन्तुमेव हि ..28.. ..
5.123.m: Therefore release all your wealth first! What is the use of vain words / being spoken? For this hand of mine twitches to strike!”

5.123.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yadyevaṃ caura tadgatvā tvaṃ pṛcchasva kuṭumbakam ..
mamapāpāṃśabhāgī tvaṃ kiṃ bhaviṣyasi kiṃ na vā..29..
5.123.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यद्येवं चौर तद्गत्वा त्वं पृच्छस्व कुटुम्बकम् ..
ममपापांशभागी त्वं किं भविष्यसि किं न वा..29..
5.123.m: The seers said: / “If so, O thief, then go and ask your family: / ‘Will you be a sharer in the portion of my sin, or not?’

5.123.s:
yadi te saṃvibhāgena pāpasyāṃśo'pi gacchati ..
tatkuruṣvāthavā pāpa durvahaṃ te bhaviṣyati .. 6.124.30 ..
5.123.d:
यदि ते संविभागेन पापस्यांशोऽपि गच्छति ..
तत्कुरुष्वाथवा पाप दुर्वहं ते भविष्यति .. 6.124.30 ..
5.123.m: If by their taking a share even a part of the sin departs, / then do it; otherwise, O sinful one, it will be unbearable for you,

5.123.s:
sakalaṃ raurave raudre patitasya sudurmate ..
vayaṃ tvā brāhmaṇaṃ matvā brūma etadasaṃśayam ..31...
5.123.d:
सकलं रौरवे रौद्रे पतितस्य सुदुर्मते ..
वयं त्वा ब्राह्मणं मत्वा ब्रूम एतदसंशयम् ..31...
5.123.m: when you have fallen entirely into the terrible Raurava hell, O evil-minded one! / Thinking you to be a brahmin, we speak this without a doubt.

5.123.s:
kṛpāviṣṭāḥ sahāsmābhiḥ sañjāte'pi sudarśane ..
munīnāṃ yatacittānāṃ darśanāddhi śubhaṃ bhavet ..32..
5.123.d:
कृपाविष्टाः सहास्माभिः सञ्जातेऽपि सुदर्शने ..
मुनीनां यतचित्तानां दर्शनाद्धि शुभं भवेत् ..32..
5.123.m: We are filled with compassion, since an auspicious darśana has occurred with us; / for through the darśana of sages whose minds are restrained, auspiciousness arises.

5.123.s:
ekaḥ pāpāni kurute phalaṃ bhuṃkte mahājanaḥ ..
bhoktāro vipramucyaṃte kartā doṣeṇa lipyate .. 33 ..
5.123.d:
एकः पापानि कुरुते फलं भुंक्ते महाजनः ..
भोक्तारो विप्रमुच्यंते कर्ता दोषेण लिप्यते .. 33 ..
5.123.m: One man commits sins, and a multitude of people enjoys the fruit; / the enjoyers are freed, but the doer is smeared with guilt.”

5.123.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sa teṣāṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā cauraḥ kiṃcidbhayānvitaḥ ..
satyametanna saṃdeho yadetairvyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ .. 34 ..
5.123.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
स तेषां तद्वचः श्रुत्वा चौरः किंचिद्भयान्वितः ..
सत्यमेतन्न संदेहो यदेतैर्व्याहृतं वचः .. 34 ..
5.123.m: Sūta said: / Hearing that speech of theirs, the robber was somewhat afraid: / “This is true, there is no doubt, this word that has been uttered by them.

5.123.s:
tasmātpṛcchāmi tadgatvā nijameva kuṭumbakam ..
yadi syātsaṃvibhāgo me pāpāṃśasya karomi vai .. 39 ..
etatkarma na gṛhṇaṃti yadi vā saṃtyajāmyaham ..
mahadbhayaṃ samutpannaṃ mama cetasi sāṃpratam ..36..
yadi yūyaṃ na cānyatra prayāsyatha munīśvarāḥ ..
palāyanaparā bhūtvā tadgatvā nijamaṃdiram ..37..
pṛcchāmi poṣyavargaṃ ca yuṣmadvākyaṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
yadi tatpātakāṃśaṃ me grahīṣyati kuṭumbakam ..
tadyuṣmākaṃ grahīṣyāmi yatkiṃcitpārśvasaṃsthitam .. 38 ..
athavā pratiṣedhaṃ me pāpasyāsya kariṣyati ..
tattyajiṣyāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ sarvānvaḥ saparicchadān .. 39 ..
5.123.d:
तस्मात्पृच्छामि तद्गत्वा निजमेव कुटुम्बकम् ..
यदि स्यात्संविभागो मे पापांशस्य करोमि वै .. 39 ..
एतत्कर्म न गृह्णंति यदि वा संत्यजाम्यहम् ..
महद्भयं समुत्पन्नं मम चेतसि सांप्रतम् ..36..
यदि यूयं न चान्यत्र प्रयास्यथ मुनीश्वराः ..
पलायनपरा भूत्वा तद्गत्वा निजमंदिरम् ..37..
पृच्छामि पोष्यवर्गं च युष्मद्वाक्यं विशेषतः ..
यदि तत्पातकांशं मे ग्रहीष्यति कुटुम्बकम् ..
तद्युष्माकं ग्रहीष्यामि यत्किंचित्पार्श्वसंस्थितम् .. 38 ..
अथवा प्रतिषेधं मे पापस्यास्य करिष्यति ..
तत्त्यजिष्याम्यसंदिग्धं सर्वान्वः सपरिच्छदान् .. 39 ..
5.123.m:
Therefore I will go and ask my own family; / if there is a division of my share of sin, indeed I shall do
this deed; or if they will not take it, I shall abandon it; / a great fear has now arisen in my heart.
If you, O lords of sages, will not go elsewhere, / having taken to flight, then, having gone to my own home,
I will ask my dependents, especially concerning your words: / ‘If my family will take that portion of my sin, / then I will take whatever is present beside you.
Or if they forbid me from this sin, / then without doubt I will let you all go, along with your belongings.’”

5.123.s:
tataste śapathānkṛtvā tasya pratyayakāraṇāt ..
tasyopari dayāṃ kṛtvā mumucustaṃ gṛhaṃ prati .. 6.124.40 ..
5.123.d:
ततस्ते शपथान्कृत्वा तस्य प्रत्ययकारणात् ..
तस्योपरि दयां कृत्वा मुमुचुस्तं गृहं प्रति .. 6.124.40 ..
5.123.m: Then, having taken oaths to convince him, / showing compassion toward him, they sent him on toward his home.

5.123.s:
so'pi gatvā'tha papraccha pragatvā pitaraṃ nijam ..
śṛṇu tāta vaco'smākaṃ tataḥ pratyuttaraṃ kuru .. 41 ..
5.123.d:
सोऽपि गत्वाऽथ पप्रच्छ प्रगत्वा पितरं निजम् ..
शृणु तात वचोऽस्माकं ततः प्रत्युत्तरं कुरु .. 41 ..
5.123.m: He too went and, having approached his father, asked: / “Listen, Father, to my words, and then make reply:

5.123.s:
yatkṛtvāhamakṛtyāni cauryādīni sahasraśaḥ ..
puṣṭiṃ karomi te nityas tadbhāgaste'sti vā na vā .. 42 ..
5.123.d:
यत्कृत्वाहमकृत्यानि चौर्यादीनि सहस्रशः ..
पुष्टिं करोमि ते नित्यस् तद्भागस्तेऽस्ति वा न वा .. 42 ..
5.123.m: Since, having committed thousands of wrong deeds, such as theft and the like, / I nourish you constantly, do you have a share of that or not?

5.123.s:
pāpasya mama prabrūhi pṛcchato'tra yathātatham ..
atra me saṃśayo jātastasmācchīghraṃ prakīrtaya .. 43 ..
5.123.d:
पापस्य मम प्रब्रूहि पृच्छतोऽत्र यथातथम् ..
अत्र मे संशयो जातस्तस्माच्छीघ्रं प्रकीर्तय .. 43 ..
5.123.m: Tell me truly as I ask here concerning my sin; / a doubt has arisen in me here, therefore declare it quickly!”

5.123.s:
.. pitovāca ..
bālye putra mayā nītastvaṃ puṣṭiṃ vyākulātmanā ..
śubhā'śubhāni kṛtyāni kṛtvā snigdhena cetasā .. 44 ..
5.123.d:
.. पितोवाच ..
बाल्ये पुत्र मया नीतस्त्वं पुष्टिं व्याकुलात्मना ..
शुभाऽशुभानि कृत्यानि कृत्वा स्निग्धेन चेतसा .. 44 ..
5.123.m: The father said: / “In childhood, my son, you were brought to nourishment by me with an anxious heart, / performing good and bad deeds with an affectionate mind.

5.123.s:
etadarthaṃ punaryena vārdhakye samupasthite ...
gāṃ pālayasi bhūyo'pi kṛtvā karma śubhā'śubham .. 45 ..
5.123.d:
एतदर्थं पुनर्येन वार्धक्ये समुपस्थिते ...
गां पालयसि भूयोऽपि कृत्वा कर्म शुभाऽशुभम् .. 45 ..
5.123.m: For this reason, however, when old age has arrived, / you again protect the earth, performing good and bad deeds.

5.123.s:
na tasya vidyate bhāgastava svalpo'pi putraka ..
śubhasya vā'tha pāpasya sāṃprataṃ ca tathā mama .. 46 ..
5.123.d:
न तस्य विद्यते भागस्तव स्वल्पोऽपि पुत्रक ..
शुभस्य वाऽथ पापस्य सांप्रतं च तथा मम .. 46 ..
5.123.m: Not even the slightest share of that belongs to you, dear son, / whether good or sin, nor does it belong to me at present.

5.123.s:
ātmanaiva kṛtaṃ karma svayamevopabhujyate ..
śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ bhoktāronyajanāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 47 ..
5.123.d:
आत्मनैव कृतं कर्म स्वयमेवोपभुज्यते ..
शुभं वा यदि वा पापं भोक्तारोन्यजनाः स्मृताः .. 47 ..
5.123.m: An action done by oneself is experienced by oneself alone, / whether good or sinful; other people are considered [merely] enjoyers.

5.123.s:
sādhutvenātha cauryeṇa kṛṣyā vā vāṇijena vā ..
tvamupānayase bhojyaṃ na me cintā prajāyate .. 48 ..
5.123.d:
साधुत्वेनाथ चौर्येण कृष्या वा वाणिजेन वा ..
त्वमुपानयसे भोज्यं न मे चिन्ता प्रजायते .. 48 ..
5.123.m: Whether by honesty, or theft, or farming, or trade, / you bring food, no concern arises in me.

5.123.s:
tasmānnaitaddhṛdi sthāpyaṃ karmaniṃdyaṃ kariṣyasi ..
yattasyāṃśaṃ prabhoktā tvaṃ vayaṃ sarve prabhuṃjakāḥ.. 49 ..
5.123.d:
तस्मान्नैतद्धृदि स्थाप्यं कर्मनिंद्यं करिष्यसि ..
यत्तस्यांशं प्रभोक्ता त्वं वयं सर्वे प्रभुंजकाः.. 49 ..
5.123.m: Therefore, you should not hold this in your heart, that 'You will perform a censurable act / of which you will enjoy a share, while all of us are consumers.'

5.123.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sa etadvacanaṃ śrutvā vyākulenānttarātmanā ..
papraccha mātaraṃ gatvā tamevārthaṃ prayatnataḥ ..6.124.50...
5.123.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
स एतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा व्याकुलेनान्त्तरात्मना ..
पप्रच्छ मातरं गत्वा तमेवार्थं प्रयत्नतः ..6.124.50...
5.123.m: Sūta said: / Having heard these words, with an inner soul distressed, / he went and questioned his mother regarding the very same matter with great effort.

5.123.s:
tatastayāpi taccoktaṃ yatpitrā tasya jalpitam ..
asāmānyaṃ śubhe pāpe kṛtye tasya dvijottamāḥ ..51...
5.123.d:
ततस्तयापि तच्चोक्तं यत्पित्रा तस्य जल्पितम् ..
असामान्यं शुभे पापे कृत्ये तस्य द्विजोत्तमाः ..51...
5.123.m: Then she too said to him that which was uttered by his father: / 'There is no sharing in his good or sinful deed, O best of twice-born.'

5.123.s:
tataḥ papraccha tāṃ bhāryāṃ gatvā duḥkhasamanvitaḥ ..
sā'pyuvāca tatastādṛkpāpaṃ gurujanodbhavam .. 52 ..
5.123.d:
ततः पप्रच्छ तां भार्यां गत्वा दुःखसमन्वितः ..
साऽप्युवाच ततस्तादृक्पापं गुरुजनोद्भवम् .. 52 ..
5.123.m: Then, filled with sorrow, he went and questioned that wife of his; / she too then spoke similarly regarding sin originating from the elders.

5.123.s:
tataḥ sa śokasaṃtaptaḥ paścāttāpena saṃyutaḥ ..
garhayanneva cātmānaṃ yayau te yatra tāpasāḥ ..53..
5.123.d:
ततः स शोकसंतप्तः पश्चात्तापेन संयुतः ..
गर्हयन्नेव चात्मानं ययौ ते यत्र तापसाः ..53..
5.123.m: Then, tormented by grief and accompanied by remorse, / constantly reproaching himself, he went to where those ascetics were.

5.123.s:
tataḥ praṇamya tānsarvānkṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ.
gamyatāṃ gamyatāṃ viprāḥ kṣamyatāṃ kṣamyatāṃ mama .. 54 ..
5.123.d:
ततः प्रणम्य तान्सर्वान्कृतांजलिपुटः स्थितः.
गम्यतां गम्यतां विप्राः क्षम्यतां क्षम्यतां मम .. 54 ..
5.123.m: Then, bowing down to all of them, he stood with folded hands: / 'Go, go, O brahmins! Pardon, pardon me!

5.123.s:
yanmayā maurkhyamāsthāya yuṣmannirbhartsanā kṛtā ..
supāpmanā vimūḍhena tasmātkāryā kṣamādya me .. 55 ..
5.123.d:
यन्मया मौर्ख्यमास्थाय युष्मन्निर्भर्त्सना कृता ..
सुपाप्मना विमूढेन तस्मात्कार्या क्षमाद्य मे .. 55 ..
5.123.m: Since, resorting to foolishness, an insult was committed by me, / a great sinner and utterly deluded, therefore patience must be granted to me today.

5.123.s:
yuṣmadīyaṃ vacaḥ kṛtsnaṃ madgurubhyāṃ prajalpitam ..
bhāryayā ca dvijaśreṣṭhāstena me duḥkhamāgatam..56..
5.123.d:
युष्मदीयं वचः कृत्स्नं मद्गुरुभ्यां प्रजल्पितम् ..
भार्यया च द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तेन मे दुःखमागतम्..56..
5.123.m: All your words were repeated by my parents / and by my wife, O best of twice-born; because of that, sorrow has come upon me.

5.123.s:
tasmātkurvaṃtu me sarve prasādaṃ munisattamāḥ ..
upadeśapradānena yena pāpaṃ kṣapāmyaham ..57..
5.123.d:
तस्मात्कुर्वंतु मे सर्वे प्रसादं मुनिसत्तमाः ..
उपदेशप्रदानेन येन पापं क्षपाम्यहम् ..57..
5.123.m: Therefore let all of you grant me favor, O best of sages, / by giving instruction through which I may destroy my sin.

5.123.s:
mayā karma kṛtaṃ niṃdyaṃ sadaiva dvijasattamāḥ..
striyo'pi ca dvijeṃdrāśca tāpasāśca viśeṣataḥ ..58..
5.123.d:
मया कर्म कृतं निंद्यं सदैव द्विजसत्तमाः..
स्त्रियोऽपि च द्विजेंद्राश्च तापसाश्च विशेषतः ..58..
5.123.m: Blameworthy action was constantly performed by me, O best of twice-born: / women, and chiefs of twice-born, and ascetics in particular.

5.123.s:
ye ye dīnatarā lokā na samarthāḥ prayodhitum ..
te mayā muṣitāḥ sarve na samarthāḥ kadācana ..59..
5.123.d:
ये ये दीनतरा लोका न समर्थाः प्रयोधितुम् ..
ते मया मुषिताः सर्वे न समर्थाः कदाचन ..59..
5.123.m: Whosoever were wretched people, unable to fight back, / all of them were robbed by me, never those who were powerful.

5.123.s:
kuṭumbārthaṃ vimūḍhena sādhusaṃgavivarjinā ..
yathaiva paṭhatā śāstraṃ tanme'dya patitaṃ hṛdi ..6.124.60...
5.123.d:
कुटुम्बार्थं विमूढेन साधुसंगविवर्जिना ..
यथैव पठता शास्त्रं तन्मेऽद्य पतितं हृदि ..6.124.60...
5.123.m: Deluded for the sake of family, bereft of company of the virtuous— / just as if one were reading scripture, that has fallen upon my heart today.

5.123.s:
yadi na syādbhavadbhirme darśanaṃ cādya sattamāḥ ..
tadanyānyapi pāpāni kartāhaṃ syāṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 61 ..
5.123.d:
यदि न स्याद्भवद्भिर्मे दर्शनं चाद्य सत्तमाः ..
तदन्यान्यपि पापानि कर्ताहं स्यां न संशयः .. 61 ..
5.123.m: If my darśana with you had not occurred today, O best of beings, / then I would be a committer of yet other sins; there is no doubt.

5.123.s:
teṣāṃ madhyagataścāsītpulaho nāma sanmuniḥ ..
hāsyaśīlaḥ sa taṃ prāha viplavārthaṃ dvijottamam .. .. 62 ..
5.123.d:
तेषां मध्यगतश्चासीत्पुलहो नाम सन्मुनिः ..
हास्यशीलः स तं प्राह विप्लवार्थं द्विजोत्तमम् .. .. 62 ..
5.123.m: And in their midst was a good sage named Pulaha; / fond of jesting, he said to that best of twice-born for the sake of confusion:

5.123.s:
ahaṃ te kīrtayiṣyāmi mantramekaṃ suśobhanam ..
yaṃ dhyāyañjapyamānastvaṃ siddhiṃ yāsyasi śāśvatīm .. 63 ..
5.123.d:
अहं ते कीर्तयिष्यामि मन्त्रमेकं सुशोभनम् ..
यं ध्यायञ्जप्यमानस्त्वं सिद्धिं यास्यसि शाश्वतीम् .. 63 ..
5.123.m: 'I will proclaim to you a very auspicious mantra, / meditating on which and reciting it, you will attain eternal perfection.

5.123.s:
jāṭaghoṭetimantro'yaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakaḥ .. (ṭi. jāṭaghoṭā = jātigotra?)
tamenaṃ japa vipra tvaṃ divārātramataṃdritaḥ .. 64 ..
5.123.d:
जाटघोटेतिमन्त्रोऽयं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकः .. (टि. जाटघोटा = जातिगोत्र?)
तमेनं जप विप्र त्वं दिवारात्रमतंद्रितः .. 64 ..
5.123.m: This mantra "jāṭaghoṭā" is the granter of all perfections; / mutter this, O brahmin, day and night without wearying.

5.123.s: tato yāsyasi saṃsiddhiṃ durlabhāṃ tridaśairapi .. 65 ..
5.123.d: ततो यास्यसि संसिद्धिं दुर्लभां त्रिदशैरपि .. 65 ..
5.123.m: Then you will attain complete perfection, difficult to attain even for the thirty [gods].'

5.123.s:
evamuktvātha te viprāstīrthayātrāṃ tato yayuḥ ..
so'pi tatraiva caurastu sthito japaparāyaṇaḥ .. 66 ..
5.123.d:
एवमुक्त्वाथ ते विप्रास्तीर्थयात्रां ततो ययुः ..
सोऽपि तत्रैव चौरस्तु स्थितो जपपरायणः .. 66 ..
5.123.m: Having spoken thus, those brahmins then departed on their pilgrimage to sacred fords; / he too, the thief, remained right there, devoted to muttering [the mantra].

5.123.s:
ananyamanasā tena prārabdhaḥ sa tadā japaḥ ..
yathā'bhavatsamādhistho yenāvasthāṃ parāṃ gataḥ .. 67 ..
5.123.d:
अनन्यमनसा तेन प्रारब्धः स तदा जपः ..
यथाऽभवत्समाधिस्थो येनावस्थां परां गतः .. 67 ..
5.123.m: With an undistracted mind, that repetition was then begun by him, / in such a way that he became absorbed in samādhi, whereby he attained the supreme state.

5.123.s:
tasyaivaṃ smaramāṇasya taṃ mantraṃ brāhmaṇasya ca ..
niścalatvaṃ gataḥ kāyaḥ kārye ca niścalaḥ sthitaḥ .. 68 ..
5.123.d:
तस्यैवं स्मरमाणस्य तं मन्त्रं ब्राह्मणस्य च ..
निश्चलत्वं गतः कायः कार्ये च निश्चलः स्थितः .. 68 ..
5.123.m: As he, the brahmin, was thus remembering that mantra, / his body attained immobility, and he remained motionless in his undertaking.

5.123.s:
tataḥ kālena mahatā valmīkena samāvṛtaḥ ..
samaṃtādbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā dhyānasthasya mahātmanaḥ .. 69 ..
5.123.d:
ततः कालेन महता वल्मीकेन समावृतः ..
समंताद्ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठा ध्यानस्थस्य महात्मनः .. 69 ..
5.123.m: Then, after a great length of time, he was covered all around by an anthill, / O best of brahmins, as that great-souled one remained in meditation.

5.123.s:
tau mātāpitarau tasya sā ca bhāryā manasvinī ..
yātā mṛtyuvaśaṃ sarve tamanveṣya prayatnataḥ .. 6.124.70 ..
5.123.d:
तौ मातापितरौ तस्य सा च भार्या मनस्विनी ..
याता मृत्युवशं सर्वे तमन्वेष्य प्रयत्नतः .. 6.124.70 ..
5.123.m: Both his parents and that high-minded wife, / having searched for him diligently, all fell under the power of death.

5.123.s:
na vijñātaśca tatrasthaḥ saṃnyastaḥ sa mahāvrataḥ ..
saṃsārabhāvanirmuktastasmānmunisamāgamāt . 71 ..
5.123.d:
न विज्ञातश्च तत्रस्थः संन्यस्तः स महाव्रतः ..
संसारभावनिर्मुक्तस्तस्मान्मुनिसमागमात् . 71 ..
5.123.m: And he, remaining there, was not noticed; renounced, of great vows, / freed from the feeling of worldly existence because of that meeting with the sages.

5.123.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya tena mārgeṇa te punaḥ ..
tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena munayaḥ samupasthitāḥ .. 72 ..
5.123.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य तेन मार्गेण ते पुनः ..
तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगेन मुनयः समुपस्थिताः .. 72 ..
5.123.m: Then, after some time, by that same path again, / the sages arrived in the course of their pilgrimage to sacred fords.

5.123.s:
procuścaitaddvijāḥ sthānaṃ yatra caureṇa saṃgamaḥ ..
āsīdvastena raudreṇa brāhmaṇacchadmadhāriṇā .. 73 ..
5.123.d:
प्रोचुश्चैतद्द्विजाः स्थानं यत्र चौरेण संगमः ..
आसीद्वस्तेन रौद्रेण ब्राह्मणच्छद्मधारिणा .. 73 ..
5.123.m: And the twice-born said: 'This is the place where the encounter with the thief / occurred, with that terrible one wearing the disguise of a brahmin.'

5.123.s:
tato valmīkamadhyasthaṃ śuśruvurnisvanaṃ ca te ..
jāṭaghoṭetimaṃtrasya tasyaiva ca mahātmanaḥ .. 74 ..
5.123.d:
ततो वल्मीकमध्यस्थं शुश्रुवुर्निस्वनं च ते ..
जाटघोटेतिमंत्रस्य तस्यैव च महात्मनः .. 74 ..
5.123.m: Then they heard a sound from within the anthill, / of the mantra "jāṭaghoṭā", belonging to that very same great-souled one.

5.123.s:
atha bhūmyāṃ prahārāste sasvanuḥ sarvatodiśam ..
te valmīkaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā taṃ cauraṃ tasya madhyagam .. 75 ..
5.123.d:
अथ भूम्यां प्रहारास्ते सस्वनुः सर्वतोदिशम् ..
ते वल्मीकं ततो दृष्ट्वा तं चौरं तस्य मध्यगम् .. 75 ..
5.123.m: Then strikes upon the ground resounded in all directions; / then, having seen the anthill and that thief situated in its midst,

5.123.s:
japamānaṃ tu taṃ mantraṃ pulahena niveditaḥ ..
hāsyarūpeṇa yastasya siddhiṃ ca dvijasattamāḥ .. 76 ..
5.123.d:
जपमानं तु तं मन्त्रं पुलहेन निवेदितः ..
हास्यरूपेण यस्तस्य सिद्धिं च द्विजसत्तमाः .. 76 ..
5.123.m: muttering that mantra which had been taught by Pulaha / in the form of a joke, and [seeing] his perfection, O best of twice-born—

5.123.s:
yadvā satyamidaṃ proktamācāryaiḥ śāstradṛṣṭibhiḥ ..
stokaṃ siddhikṛte tasya yasmātsiddhirupasthitā .. 77 ..
5.123.d:
यद्वा सत्यमिदं प्रोक्तमाचार्यैः शास्त्रदृष्टिभिः ..
स्तोकं सिद्धिकृते तस्य यस्मात्सिद्धिरुपस्थिता .. 77 ..
5.123.m: Or rather, this was truthfully spoken by the teachers who see through the scriptures: / a little is sufficient for perfection, since perfection was attained by him.

5.123.s:
mantre tīrthe dvije deve daivajñe bheṣaje gurau ..
yādṛśī bhāvanā yasya siddhirbhavati tādṛśī .. .. 78 ..
5.123.d:
मन्त्रे तीर्थे द्विजे देवे दैवज्ञे भेषजे गुरौ ..
यादृशी भावना यस्य सिद्धिर्भवति तादृशी .. .. 78 ..
5.123.m: Toward a mantra, a sacred ford, a twice-born, a deity, an astrologer, medicine, and a guru— / whatever kind of mental disposition one has, such perfection comes to be.

5.123.s:
atha taṃ vīkṣya saṃsiddhaṃ kumantreṇāpi taskaram ..
te viprā vismayāviṣṭāḥ kṛpāviṣṭā viśeṣataḥ .. 79 ..
5.123.d:
अथ तं वीक्ष्य संसिद्धं कुमन्त्रेणापि तस्करम् ..
ते विप्रा विस्मयाविष्टाः कृपाविष्टा विशेषतः .. 79 ..
5.123.m: Then, seeing that thief accomplished even by means of a bad mantra, / those brahmins were filled with wonder, and especially filled with compassion.

5.123.s: samādhyarhaistato dravyaistailaistadbheṣajairapi .. 6.124.80 ..
5.123.d: समाध्यर्हैस्ततो द्रव्यैस्तैलैस्तद्भेषजैरपि .. 6.124.80 ..
5.123.m: Then, with substances fit for samādhi, with oils and with remedies,

5.123.s:
mamardustasya tadgātraṃ samādhisthaṃ ciraṃ dvijāḥ ..
tataḥ sa cetanāṃ labdhā ālokya ca muhurmuhuḥ ..
provāca vismayāviṣṭastānmunīnprakṛtāniti .. 81 ..
5.123.d:
ममर्दुस्तस्य तद्गात्रं समाधिस्थं चिरं द्विजाः ..
ततः स चेतनां लब्धा आलोक्य च मुहुर्मुहुः ..
प्रोवाच विस्मयाविष्टस्तान्मुनीन्प्रकृतानिति .. 81 ..
5.123.m: the twice-born massaged his body, which had been in samādhi for a long time. / Then, having regained consciousness and looking again and again, / filled with amazement, he spoke to those original sages thus:

5.123.s:
.. lohajaṃgha uvāca .. ..
kimarthaṃ na gatā yūyaṃ mayā muktā dvijottamāḥ ..
nāhaṃ kiṃcidgrahīṣyāmi yuṣmadīyaṃ kathaṃcana ..
kuṭuṃbārthaṃ yatastasmādvrajadhvaṃ svecchayā'dhunā .. 82 ..
5.123.d:
.. लोहजंघ उवाच .. ..
किमर्थं न गता यूयं मया मुक्ता द्विजोत्तमाः ..
नाहं किंचिद्ग्रहीष्यामि युष्मदीयं कथंचन ..
कुटुंबार्थं यतस्तस्माद्व्रजध्वं स्वेच्छयाऽधुना .. 82 ..
5.123.m: Lohajaṅgha said: / 'Why have you not gone, having been released by me, O best of twice-born? / I will not take anything belonging to you by any means. / Since [I acted] for the sake of family, therefore depart now according to your desire.'

5.123.s:
.. munaya ūcuḥ.. ..
cirakālādvayaṃ prāptāḥ punarbhrāṃtvā'tra kānane ..
samādhisthena na jñātaḥ kālo'tītastvayā bahu .. 83 ..
5.123.d:
.. मुनय ऊचुः.. ..
चिरकालाद्वयं प्राप्ताः पुनर्भ्रांत्वाऽत्र कानने ..
समाधिस्थेन न ज्ञातः कालोऽतीतस्त्वया बहु .. 83 ..
5.123.m: The sages said: / 'We have arrived after a long time, having wandered in this forest again. / Remaining in samādhi, the passage of much time was not noticed by you.

5.123.s:
tau mātāpitarau vṛddhau tvayā muktau kṣayaṃ gatau .
tvaṃ ca saṃsiddhimāpannaḥ parāmasmatprasādataḥ .. ..84..
5.123.d:
तौ मातापितरौ वृद्धौ त्वया मुक्तौ क्षयं गतौ .
त्वं च संसिद्धिमापन्नः परामस्मत्प्रसादतः .. ..84..
5.123.m: Those elderly parents, left behind by you, have gone to destruction; / and you have attained supreme perfection by our grace.

5.123.s:
valmīkāṃtaḥ sthito yasmātsaṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ ..
valmīkirnāma vikhyātastasmālloke bhaviṣyasi.. 85 ..
5.123.d:
वल्मीकांतः स्थितो यस्मात्संसिद्धिं परमां गतः ..
वल्मीकिर्नाम विख्यातस्तस्माल्लोके भविष्यसि.. 85 ..
5.123.m: Because you remained inside an anthill and attained supreme perfection, / you will therefore become renowned in the world by the name Valmīki.

5.123.s:
atrasthena yato muṣṭāstvayā lokāḥ purā dvija ..
mukhārākhyaṃ tatastīrthametatkhyātiṃ gamiṣyati..86..
5.123.d:
अत्रस्थेन यतो मुष्टास्त्वया लोकाः पुरा द्विज ..
मुखाराख्यं ततस्तीर्थमेतत्ख्यातिं गमिष्यति..86..
5.123.m: Because people were robbed by you formerly while staying here, O twice-born, / therefore this sacred ford will attain renown under the name Mukhāra.'

5.123.s:
ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti śrāvaṇyāṃ śraddhayā dvijāḥ..
kṣālayiṣyaṃti te pāpaṃ caurya karmasamudbhavam ..87..
5.123.d:
येऽत्र स्नानं करिष्यंति श्रावण्यां श्रद्धया द्विजाः..
क्षालयिष्यंति ते पापं चौर्य कर्मसमुद्भवम् ..87..
5.123.m: Those brahmins who will take a ritual ablution here with faith on the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa / will wash away the sin born of deeds of theft.

5.123.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvātha te viprāstamāmaṃtrya muniṃ tataḥ ..
praṇatāstena saṃjagmurvāṃchitāśāṃ tataḥ param .. 88 ..
5.123.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वाथ ते विप्रास्तमामंत्र्य मुनिं ततः ..
प्रणतास्तेन संजग्मुर्वांछिताशां ततः परम् .. 88 ..
5.123.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, those vipras bid farewell to that sage; / bowed to by him, they then departed to the quarter they desired.

5.123.s: tapaḥsthaḥ so'pi tatraiva vālmīkiriti yaḥ smṛtaḥ . 89 ..
5.123.d: तपःस्थः सोऽपि तत्रैव वाल्मीकिरिति यः स्मृतः . 89 ..
5.123.m: He also remained engaged in austerity right there, who is remembered as Vālmīki.

5.123.s:
munīnāṃ pravaraḥ śreṣṭhaḥ saṃjātaśca tataḥ param ..
adyāpi tiṣṭhate mūrtaḥ sa tatrastho munīśvaraḥ .. 6.124.90 ..
5.123.d:
मुनीनां प्रवरः श्रेष्ठः संजातश्च ततः परम् ..
अद्यापि तिष्ठते मूर्तः स तत्रस्थो मुनीश्वरः .. 6.124.90 ..
5.123.m: And thereafter he became the foremost, the best among sages. / Even today that lord of sages stands there in bodily form.

5.123.s:
yastaṃ prapūjayedbhaktyā sa kavirjāyate bhuvam..
aṣṭamyāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ .. 91 ..
5.123.d:
यस्तं प्रपूजयेद्भक्त्या स कविर्जायते भुवम्..
अष्टम्यां च विशेषेण सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः .. 91 ..
5.123.m: Whoever worships him with devotion on earth becomes a poet, / especially on the eighth day, fully endowed with faith.

5.123.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye mukhāratīrthotpattivarṇanaṃnāma caturviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 124 ..
5.123.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये मुखारतीर्थोत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम चतुर्विंशत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 124 ..
5.123.m: Thus ends the one hundred twenty-fourth chapter, entitled “Description of the Origin of the Mukhāratīrtha,” in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
